Unlike many of his players, Michael Carrick has personal experience of the special nights as a Manchester United player at Old Trafford in the Champions League. This was scarcely one of them, but if Carrick had compiled a list of things he wanted from the evening, this must have ticked nearly every box. A perfect night? “Yeah, I think so,” he said.

The fixture list made it a low-key comeback to the Champions League but Carrick was able to rest four players ahead of the Manchester derby, take off five more and chalk up a comfortable win. “Some of the football we played was really good,” said Carrick. “We just did a lot of good things.” Some players benefited. Matheus Cunha, who was fortunate to avoid a late red card for a studs-up challenge on Erivaldo Almeida, surely needed his first goal of the season. Benjamin Sesko marked his first start of the campaign with a second goal in a week.

open image in gallery Bruno Fernandes was instrumental as United put four past Sabah ( Reuters )

In a sense, though, the most meaningful goal came from Bruno Fernandes. The captain was nominated for the Ballon d’Or even after a campaign when United were not in any continental competition. He showed a loyalty to United during their European exile. More than any other player, he dragged them back into the Champions League. It was fitting he scored on their return. Fernandes being Fernandes, it was also typical he was not among the rested or the removed.

Carrick has rarely needed to rotate since he took charge. Given this season’s greater workload, this was something of a learning exercise. Patrick Dorgu played left-back for the first time under Carrick, excelled in attack and played a part in the first two goals, but revealed defensive deficiencies. Noussair Mazraoui, brought back in for Diogo Dalot, seemed to have a point to prove and looked lively going forward. A fit-again Mason Mount made a belated first appearance of the campaign in the second half. Andrey Santos, dropped after his ill-fated debut at Hull, got the final half-hour. The youngsters Harry Amass and Shea Lacey appeared for the last 20 minutes.

By then, the game was won. It could have been more emphatic but it was still United’s biggest Champions League victory since 2020’s 5-0 rout of RB Leipzig; yet that also reflects the reality they have sat out many a European night since then. As they became the first English club to play 300 games in the European Cup, it was also their first since 2023.

Carrick gave Luke Shaw the night off altogether, while United’s lead allowed Harry Maguire, Marcus Rashford and Diogo Dalot to remain on the bench. Later, Youri Tielemans, Kobbie Mainoo, Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Dorgu joined them there.

The first two goals featured Dorgu’s forays forward. “Pat played every so well, he was a big threat,” said Carrick. For the breakthrough, and after Sabah had made a fine start, the overlapping left-back crossed for Cunha to finish at the near post. The Brazilian had made a slow start to the season as a supposed centre-forward. Perhaps it was no coincidence he scored when in a deeper role. He looked better operating off the left, with Dorgu’s runs outside him allowing him to come infield.

open image in gallery Fernandes bagged a second as Sabah fell apart at the back ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Sesko added a third shortly before half-time ( Reuters )

Then came a quickfire double just before the break. Tielemans span to pass and Fernandes angled his shot in perfectly. It reinforced the sense two creative, intelligent footballers have the potential to combine well.

The third goal came when Mbeumo sent Sesko in behind the Sabah defence. He strolled past goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov to finish. “Ben gives us a different kind of threat,” said Carrick. Sesko’s shin problems have restricted his minutes this season and he had gone off before United added a fourth.

Lisandro Martinez supplied the close-range finish after a cheeky chipped free kick from Fernandes and a deft backheel from the substitute Joshua Zirkzee. United rejected a deadline-day attempt from Everton to take him on loan and Zirkzee only looks a back-up but he was prominent, seeking to make the most of his longest outing of the season.

open image in gallery Lisandro Martinez scored a fourth to cap a comfortable win ( PA Wire )

For Sabah, it was a night to savour for other reasons. Their Champions League run began in July, before the World Cup finished. This was their second game of the campaign in England: the first, against Welsh champions The New Saints, was in Oswestry, before a crowd of 1,179. There were rather more at Old Trafford for the biggest game in the Azerbaijani champions’ history.

They were only founded in 2017. They have come a long way in a short time and the rank outsiders perhaps ought to have had a goal to celebrate. But when Joy-Lance Mickels headed Kaheem Parris’ cross into the side-netting, the Rwandan striker was unable to believe he did not equalise. Later the substitute Orphe Mbina headed against the bar.

Sabah showed verve to accompany their counter-attacking pace. “A clean sheet was important,” said Carrick, but it contained elements of fortune. United’s next European tie will provide a greater barometer of their prospects.

Visiting Atletico Madrid will be a different kind of learning exercise about Carrick and his team. Stiffer tests await, but United have already won as many Champions League games as they did in their last campaign in this competition: one.

News.content:

At The Chalk Freehouse in Chelsea, Tom Kerridge has decided that simply letting the dog into the pub is no longer enough: now it gets its own Sunday lunch.

“The Dog’s Dinner”, launched at the end of August and running every Sunday through autumn, is a complimentary roast for dogs whose owners are eating from the pub’s Sunday menu. Developed with fresh dog food brand Butternut Box, it includes pork, dog-friendly roast potatoes, crushed carrot and Yorkshire pudding. The human sitting opposite is likely to be eating 30-day dry-aged rib-eye. Nobody, human or otherwise, needs to suffer the indignity of looking longingly at anybody else’s plate.

The small print adds that “cats and rabbits are subject to the manager’s discretion”, although the pub says none has yet tested the policy.

open image in gallery Hot dog: some will be reeling from the prospect of dogs at dinner tables – and others will be happily helping their pet up to their throne ( Getty )

It would once have been enough for a restaurant to describe itself as dog-friendly, which generally meant a bowl of water and an understanding waiter. Perhaps a biscuit. Now the dog is not merely welcome; the dog has a menu.

At Los Mochis, the Japanese-Mexican restaurant in Notting Hill and the City, every August is dog month. This year’s menu included treats devised especially for canine customers, among them chef Leo’s signature “doggy caviar”, kibble made from sturgeon caviar oil but without the added salt. Everything is made in-house, gluten and nut-free and, according to the restaurant, takes months to develop.

At Roe in Canary Wharf, dogs can order from a “Dogtail List”: an £8 canine steak, £5 rosé “wine” made with elderflower, linden blossom and ginseng and £5 British-brewed dog “beer”. Should the evening have run away with them, there is also a £3 puppuccino listed, naturally, under “digestif”.

Knightsbridge goes further. At the Egerton House Hotel, £30 buys the dog an afternoon tea of chicken and beef meatloaf, homemade biscuits and carrot cupcake, all prepared to order. For £550, afternoon tea can be followed by a three-hour portrait sitting and an A4 watercolour to take home.

There are two ways of responding to all of this. The first is to conclude that society has finally lost its mind. The second is to bring your dog along, if you have one.

open image in gallery Pavlovian paradise: Alby, my Miniature Dachshund, keeps a close eye on the cupcake situation ( Hannah Twiggs )

I do, which makes it harder to summon much outrage at the prospect of someone cooking him lunch. Besides, beneath the doggy caviar and faux wine is a straightforward calculation. Britain has a lot of dogs. Their owners like going out. They’d rather not choose between the two.

There are now an estimated 15.5 million dogs in the UK, 3 million more than in 2021. Some 41 per cent of households have one, rising to 58 per cent among 25- to 34-year-olds. In London, 49 per cent of households have a dog.

They increasingly come with us. PDSA research found that 48 per cent of pet owners like taking their animal on days out, 38 per cent take them on holiday and 36 per cent take them along when socialising. Restaurants, which have seldom allowed a large pool of potential customers to go unmonetised for long, have noticed.

At The Cavendish in Marylebone, they added a dog menu five years ago, when customers began ordering from the human menu for their canine guests.

“There were a couple of guests ordering plain burger patties or plain steak for their dogs,” they told me. “We felt that we could do something specific like a canine menu, to create a full experience for guests who would like to bring their dogs to the pub – and our crowd are totally dog people.”

There was another motivation. Staff wanted dogs themselves but the hours made ownership difficult. “So we introduced something that could let us pet dogs more.”

The menu is not a case of emptying a tin into one of the restaurant’s nicer bowls. The Cavendish uses meat left from its roasts, boiling or roasting it separately, and says it follows veterinary guidelines on macronutrients. There are chicken and beef dishes, plus a frozen banana and natural yoghurt treat in summer.

“The feeling of using whole ingredients to cook for dogs is more special than something that a pet owner can just buy at home,” they said. “It’s like, why would I go to a restaurant to eat a meal deal? We want the dining experience to be as special for dogs.”

Los Mochis has arrived at much the same place from a glossier direction. Dogs were not retrofitted to the brand: the restaurant was named after founder Markus Thesleff’s dog Mochi, whose likeness appears in a mural at its Notting Hill site.

“It felt very natural for us that a restaurant named after a dog should be somewhere that dogs themselves feel completely at home,” says Thesleff.

For Dog Month, all money raised goes to Silver Fox Rescue.

“But, more importantly, we wanted to create something that felt genuinely special rather than an afterthought,” it says. “The team spends months developing and perfecting the menu, making sure that every element is both appropriate for dogs and as delicious as we can possibly make it.”

It felt very natural for us that a restaurant named after a dog should be somewhere that dogs themselves feel completely at home Markus Thesleff, owner of Los Mochis

Still, dismiss this entirely as branding and you miss what the restaurants are seeing. Los Mochis says customers increasingly choose it because dogs can come too. The Cavendish says walk-ins surprised by the dog menu often return so the dog can eat properly next time. Some arrive for grander occasions.

“We see around more than a dozen birthdays for dogs a month,” Thesleff says, adding that owners specify the breed when booking so staff can allocate a suitable table.

The Cavendish was recently named one of six finalists in the Great British Pub Awards’ best pub for dogs category (yes, that’s actually a thing) and says it is the only London pub on the shortlist. More revealing are the regulars.

open image in gallery Pour-rover: dogs are increasingly being treated as diners in their own right ( Getty )

One was Winston, an enormous Bernedoodle whose American owners lived for a time in Marylebone. “Winston would somehow only be able to eat food from our dog menu” because of an appetite issue, they said. “We’ve even opened the venue early in order to feed Winston and chat with his owners.”

The dogs themselves soon learn the arrangement. “We’ve had dogs pull their unknowing dog walkers into the pub for pets with the staff who they recognise, as their owners bring them here regularly – our definition of a dog-regular!”

Restaurants have always survived on regulars. Apparently nobody stipulated that they needed credit cards or opposable thumbs.

The financial equation is more interesting than the price of a bowl of chicken. The Cavendish admits its dog food does not make the pub much money, but somebody celebrating their Cockapoo’s third birthday rarely orders the dog a £6 dinner and sits soberly beside it with tap water.

The dog, then, is not really the customer. Or at least not the only one. For neighbourhood restaurants and pubs, becoming the place somebody can walk into after the park, dog still attached, is worth rather more than the margin on canine ice cream. The owner stays for a drink, comes back for dinner and the dog learns where the treats are kept.

The feeling of using whole ingredients to cook for dogs is more special than something that a pet owner can just buy at home. It’s like, why would I go to a restaurant to eat a meal deal? We want the dining experience to be as special for dogs The Cavendish

Dog-friendly restaurants are hardly new, either. Jeremy King was making the case years ago. Back when he was running Bellanger and Colbert, he told Country Life: “When it comes to dogs, I so envy the French and the way that they integrate them into city life, with all their foibles and idiosyncrasies.” His Cockapoo Teddy accompanied him to work; Bellanger baked dog biscuits in its kitchen every day.

Kerridge, too, has long wanted dogs in his pubs. When the Chelsea site was announced in its previous guise as The Butcher’s Tap & Grill, he said the ambition was for a “local’s local”, whether the locals had two legs or four. “We will also be dog-friendly, so well-behaved four-legged friends are very welcome too!”

What has changed is the ceremony. A biscuit from the kitchen has become a roast dinner. A water bowl has become a drinks list. At one hotel, the dog can eat afternoon tea before sitting for its portrait. The language of eating out – menus, courses, cocktails, birthdays, dietary requirements, specials – is being extended to an animal that would, given the opportunity, also eat half a kebab it found beside a bin.

There is something ridiculous about that. But dogs are ridiculous. It’s one of their better qualities.

The more interesting question is whether making space for them makes restaurants better at the thing they’re supposed to do. Plenty of places describe themselves as dog-friendly while seating you suspiciously close to the loo. The better ones understand that the point is not really to make a fuss of the dog. It is to make the person on the other end of the lead feel welcome.

The Cavendish says owners have written letters explaining what the pub has meant to them because of relationships formed around their pets. It wants people to be able to go out and socialise without wondering whether the dog is in the way. Occasionally, staff say, the dog gets its water before the humans do.

“You think you’re just serving dog food with someone’s pint, but really, you’re providing a much-needed space for people.”

Which perhaps explains why Britain’s newest fine diner is waiting patiently beneath the table, hoping someone remembered to book the roast.

Coco Gauff was cheered on by Michelle Obama at the US Open, but it will be Elena Rybakina or Aryna Sabalenka who will become the first lady of Flushing Meadows.

American hearts were broken for a second time when Rybakina came from a set down to sink Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4, a couple of hours after Sabalenka had sent Jessica Pegula packing in her home city.

Rybakina, the 27-year-old from Kazakhstan, stole the world number one spot from Sabalenka by reaching the semi-finals, and on Saturday she will attempt to prise the US Open title from her grasp as well.

open image in gallery Rybakina defeated Sabalenka earlier this year to win her third grand slam title at the Australian Open ( Reuters )

“I feel like it was a great match, and of course, a lot of people wanted Coco to win. It’s normal. I think everyone understands,” she said.

“In the beginning I felt like it was a very nice atmosphere, and only in the end when I was up in the third set crowd really supported a lot Coco. But I tried to focus on myself and tried to not listen.”

A break of serve for 4-2 and a commanding hold to love put Gauff on the way to taking the first set, but her serve and forehand wobbles returned at precisely the wrong time to gift Rybakina the second

As the tension rose deep in the decider, a wide Gauff forehand gave Rybakina break point, which she took for 5-3, but a stunning backhand on the run, accompanied by a scream of defiance, kept the home favourite afloat.

However, a Rybakina volley in the next brought up two match points and she took the first when Gauff’s desperate overhead flew long.

Gauff, who won the title in 2023, said: “It hurts. Yeah, it’s all great, but I think the competitor in me, this is the tournament I want to perform at.

open image in gallery Gauff was bidding to reach her second US Open final ( Getty )

“I mean, I did perform, but it’s the one that you want to come out with a win.”

Sabalenka had earlier overpowered Pegula 7-5 6-2 to reach her fourth successive final here.

The two-time defending champion took her winning streak in New York to 19 matches and is now one victory away from the ‘three-peat’.

Third seed Pegula, beaten by Sabalenka in the 2024 final, had served superbly during the first set, winning 18 out of 20 points behind her first serve.

That was until 5-6, when Sabalenka suddenly unleashed three blistering returns to bring up three set points, taking the second when Pegula’s forehand fell into the net.

More break points arrived in the fourth game of the second set and a 91mph return put the top seed in total control.

A business-like victory was wrapped up in an hour and 20 minutes and celebrated with a simple clenched fist.

open image in gallery Sabalenka, right, overpowered Jessica Pegula (Yuki Iwamura/AP)

“No complaints, I’m super happy to be able to play such tennis,” said Sabalenka. “I was so desperate to win, I wanted it badly.”

Pegula, 32, is still looking for a maiden grand slam title and admitted she faced an almost impossible task with Sabalenka in that mood.

She said: “I don’t know who p****d her off today – hopefully it wasn’t me totally, but it might have been – I don’t know. She played insane. She played a super-high level.

“Honestly, I don’t really know if there was much I could do today.”

Sweden is holding an election on Sunday that will determine whether a conservative leader remains in charge and a hard-right party wins ministerial jobs for the first time, or whether the center-left returns to power.

Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson is seeking a second four-year term at the helm of the European Union nation that is also NATO’s newest member. His predecessor hopes to win the job back. The question of who will govern has taken up more space than actual policy issues.

More than 8 million people in the nation of about 10.6 million people are eligible to vote in the election for the 349-seat parliament in Stockholm, the Riksdag, which will elect the next prime minister.

Who are the contenders?

Kristersson has led Sweden since 2022 with a three-party center-right coalition. It relies on outside support from the Sweden Democrats, an anti-immigration party that has far-right roots but has moved toward the political mainstream, for a parliamentary majority. If the right is re-elected, it can expect Cabinet posts this time.

He's up against Magdalena Andersson of the center-left Social Democrats, a party that more often than not led Swedish governments since World War II. Andersson served as prime minister from 2021 until she lost power at the last election.

Experts say the campaign has been fragmented and incoherent, with policy questions such as how health care should be organized drowned out by the question of which parties will be able to put together a government.

“Crime has come down, inflation has come down. So these topics are not really what people discuss," said Zeth Isaksson, a sociologist in electoral behavior at Stockholm University. "People discuss who is going to be in government, and that’s what the election is about.”

How does it work?

There are two major political blocs: one with four parties on the right and another with four parties on the left. So the big question is not so much which party wins as which side can put together a majority. Individual parties need a minimum 4% of the vote to win parliamentary seats.

On the face of it, “it would be a sensation if the opposition parties, having been ahead in the opinion polls pretty much for four years since the last election, didn’t now win a majority,” said Nicholas Aylott, associate professor of political science at Södertörn University.

But he said that an “extremely defensive” campaign by the Social Democrats may have cost them some support, leaving some voters wondering why they should support the party. The right-wing bloc's hope of convincing voters that it's more united than its rivals may have had “a little impact,” he added.

What's different this time?

One significant thing is different in this election. The Sweden Democrats, who in 2022 took 20.5% of the vote to become the biggest party on the right, can expect Cabinet seats if power doesn't change hands.

Kristersson announced in April that his conservative Moderates would allow them into government if the right has a majority — though he would remain prime minister, even if the Sweden Democrats are the stronger party.

The Sweden Democrats were founded in the 1980s by people who had been active in right-wing extremist groups, including neo-Nazis. They toned down their rhetoric and expelled openly racist members under Jimmie Åkesson, who has led them since 2005 and overseen their growth from what was once a marginal party.

“There’s some, I won’t say fear, but trepidation, apprehension about the possibility of Sweden Democrat ministers,” Aylott said, and the Social Democrats recently have tried to exploit that.

But even as parties on the populist right gain elsewhere in Europe, for instance in a far-right triumph in a weekend state election in Germany, the election may reinforce the impression that the Sweden Democrats “have peaked to some extent,” Isaksson said.

Are Russia and Ukraine an election issue?

Not so much. “The biggest threat to Sweden’s security is from the war in Ukraine and there is almost complete consensus in Sweden about support for Ukraine and deep antipathy towards Russia,” Aylott said.

Sweden's Psychological Defense Agency said that the country's election isn't Russia's top priority, as that broad support reduces the incentive for Moscow to interfere.

However, just over a week before the election, Expo magazine published a report alleging that a civil servant working in parliament for the Sweden Democrats had spread Russian state narratives on social networks. She is the partner of the head of the party's coordination office with the government, Gustav Gellerbrant.

Gellerbrant said her posts were taken out of context and were meant as irony and sarcasm. He said he decided to go on parental leave to avoid shifting the focus of the election campaign.

Kristersson, who said that “there is no room for pro-Russian narratives in Sweden," welcomed that decision.

After decades of post-World War II neutrality and centuries of broader nonalignment with major powers, Sweden joined NATO in 2024 as the trans-Atlantic military alliance’s 32nd member. The move to join was initiated by Andersson's government after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and completed under Kristersson.

The Champions League is underway – but who is looking strongest after the first round?

The opening week of fixtures saw big wins for holders Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona, while Arsenal, Manchester City and Aston Villa earned away victories to start with three points. Liverpool defeated Atletico Madrid at home while Manchester United marked their return to the Champions League with a 4-0 win over the debutants Sabah.

Here’s how things stand in our 36-team power standings

1. Paris Saint-Germain

Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava

Fixtures: Manchester City (a), Barcelona (h), Villarreal (a), Roma (h), Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h)

The back-to-back defending champions are still the team to beat, despite their indifferent start domestically. But Luis Enrique’s team have proved over the last couple of seasons that they know how to peak at the right time. They could finish outside the top eight of this season’s group phase, as they have done over the past two years, and would still be considered favourites due to the midfield brilliance of Vitinha and Joao Neves and the attacking quality of Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Their next two fixtures away to Manchester City and at home to Barcelona are intriguing on paper, but the French champions know the real work begins in February.

open image in gallery Ferran Torres scored a hat-trick on PSG’s opening win over Slovan Bratislava ( Reuters )

2. Arsenal

Results: 1-0 vs Napoli

Fixtures: Lille (h), Bayern Munich (a), Slavia Prague (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h)

Last season’s runner-up are determined to go one better after their heartbreaking defeat on penalties to PSG last season. It remains to be seen if Mikel Arteta’s side can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League, but their unrivalled squad depth means the Gunners have a very good chance of finishing one of the top two spots in this season’s group phase. The early season form of Martin Odegaard, who can be like a new signing, could give Arsenal more of an edge in their attack.

open image in gallery Martin Odegaard has started the season in excellent form ( Reuters )

3. Barcelona

Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord

Fixtures: Galatasaray (a), PSG (a), Aston Villa (h), Sabah (a), Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h)

Arguably Europe’s in-form side after a devastating start to the season where Hansi Flick’s team have scored 22 goals in their first five games, hitting five goals in four of those matches. Despite not replacing Robert Lewandowski, aside from the free signing of Gabriel Jesus, their attack has sparked into life: Raphinha is off to a flyer while Lamine Yamal is set to return stronger after missing the end of last season with a hamstring injury. The addition of Rodri, too, gives Barcelona experience and muscle in midfield. Tougher tests await but should Barcelona continue their run through tricky tests away from home against Galatasaray and holders PSG then the LaLiga champions could find themselves at the top of this list, while inspiring confidence that they could compete for a first Champions League crown since 2015.

open image in gallery Raphinha and Barcelona have started the season on fire ( Reuters )

4. Bayern Munich

Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt

Fixtures: Viking (a), Arsenal (h), Atletico Madrid (a), Lille (a), Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h)

It felt like Bayern Munich were on the verge of a breakthrough last season after finishing second to Arsenal in the league phase and ending their hoodoo against Real Madrid in an enthralling quarter-final. The semi-final against PSG was ludicrous and perhaps showed that Vincent Kompany’s team were the finest side in Europe last season after the eventual Champions League winners. Certainly, if Harry Kane continues his astonishing rate of goalscoring and Michael Olise continues to unlock new levels of his game then Bayern will be there or thereabouts. As with PSG’s supremacy in France, their dominance of the Bundesliga is likely to give the German champions an advantage over their Premier League and Spanish rivals come April and May.

open image in gallery Harry Kane scored his first Champions League goal of the season and Michael Olise got two in the 5-0 win over Bodo ( Getty )

5. Manchester City

Results: 2-0 v Porto

Fixtures: PSG (h), AEK Athens (h), Leipzig (a), Napoli (h), Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a)

Unlike the four high-class teams above them, it feels like more of a stretch to call Manchester City contenders for this season’s Champions League. There has been so much change, particurly in the dugout with Pep Guardiola departing and Enzo Maresca ushering through a complete overhaul of City’s midfield. There is quality throughout the team, no doubt, but Guardiola won just one Champions League title in his 10 years at City, a record that many considered to be an underperformance in Europe’s top competition due to City’s dominance of the Premier League during that spell. It underlines the task facing Maresca as the Italian takes charge, but wins against PSG or Barcelona in the group phase would mark City as a threat.

open image in gallery Erling Haaland scored twice in City’s opening win at Porto ( Getty )

6. Real Madrid

Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan

Fixtures: Roma (a), RB Leipzig (h), AEK Athens (a), PSV (h), Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a)

Whatever happens, it’s going to be fun to watch with Jose Mourinho returning to the Bernabeu charged with preventing a third consecutive season without a trophy. The 15-time Champions League winners are faced with the same conundrum as last year of how to get Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr playing together in a balanced side. Real Madrid still look light midfield and missing out on Rodri, who joined Barcelona, could have made a big difference. But there is still an aura around Real Madrid in this competition, with their opening 2-1 win over Inter offering a bit of a throwback to the days of Carlo Ancelotti: Inter were in control of the first half but found themselves trailing 2-0 as Real Madrid inevitably scored from their first two shots.

open image in gallery Kylian Mbappe is out to win his first Champions League ( Getty )

7. Liverpool

Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid

Fixtures: LASK (a), Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Club Brugge (a), Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h)

Sitting outside the top tier of contenders, you’d have to say it would be a surprise for Liverpool (or any of the teams below the Reds in these rankings) to win the Champions League in their first season under Andoni Iraola. Issues in midfield and defence abound while a lack of squad depth may come back to cost them, but the one thing Liverpool have going for them is the potential of their attack, if Iraola gets a tune out of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and new signing Bradley Barcola ahead of Hugo Ekitike’s return from injury. A relatively kind fixture list helps, as does Liverpool’s record in the Champions League in recent years. It has taken PSG to knock them out in the last two seasons.

open image in gallery Alexis Mac Allister scored Liverpool’s winner in their opening victory over Atletico Madrid ( Reuters )

8. Inter Milan

Results: 1-2 v Real Madrid

Fixtures: Club Brugge (h), Shakhtar (h), Feyenoord (a), Stuttgart (h), Borussia Dortmund (a), Liverpool (h), Slovan Bratislava (a)

Memories of the last two seasons sting, with Inter beaten 5-0 by PSG in the 2025 final before being knocked out by Bodo/Glimt in last season’s knockout play-off in one of the Champions League’s biggest ever shocks. The Serie A champions remain the strongest side in Italy, whose teams struggled badly overall last season, and the tactical flexibility of their 3-5-2 with flying wing-backs and Lautaro Martinez and Marcus Thuram forming a strong front-two can offer an edge in some games. Even before the trip to the Bernabeu, Inter’s group-phase fixtures were rated as the easiest of the 36 teams in this season’s Champions League.

open image in gallery Inter were narrowly beaten by Real Madrid on the opening night ( Getty )

9. Atletico Madrid

Results: 1-2 v Liverpool

Fixtures: Manchester United (h), Stuttgart (a), Bayern Munich (h), Viking (h), PSV (a), Bodo/Glimt (a), Fenerbahce (h)

Last season’s semi-finalists have the added motivation of hosting this season’s Champions League final at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Yet it would be another colossal overachievement from Diego Simeone to get Atleti into a third Champions League final of his 15-year reign. You know what you’re going to get from a Simeone side in the Champions League - knocking out Barcelona in last season’s quarter-finals was a reminder of their ability to play up to the underdog role in the latter stages.

open image in gallery Julian Alvarez has remained at Atletico Madrid ( Getty )

10. Manchester United

Results: 4-0 v Sabah

Fixtures: Atletico Madrid (a), Como (a), Roma (h), Sporting (a), RB Leipzig (h), Bayern Munich (h), Villarreal (a)

It’s been so long since Manchester United were competitive in the Champions League and a paltry two quarter-finals since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement highlights the gap to European’s elite. Michael Carrick is now tasked with reviving one of the continent’s grandest clubs but this is also unfamiliar ground for an inexperienced coach who must now balance Premier League and European commitments. An opening 4-0 win against Sabah, the champions of Azerbaijan, means United have already equalled their total of wins from their last appearance in the Champions League two years ago, but a challenging fixture list now awaits and that will reveal United’s true level in this competition.

open image in gallery Bruno Fernandes was on target as United swept Sabah aside ( Reuters )

Get £100 off the iPhone 17 Pro

open image in gallery ( David Phelan/The Independent )

Following the announcement of the new iPhone 18 Pro, the previous model is now available with a discount at Very, Currys, Amazon and more. “Apple’s phones have immaculate build quality, exceptional components and chic design,” said tech critic David Phelan when he put the smartphone to the test.

“It’s like Apple thought about all the boxes it could, and then ticked them all,” he added. Overall, Phelan was impressed by the iPhone 17 Pro’s super-fast performance, battery life and camera capabilities. “Add in the company’s intuitive interface and you have an irresistible combination,” he said.

Fenty Beauty launches new longwear foundation

open image in gallery Helen and I tested the new foundation ahead of its release ( The Independent )

In non-tech news, Helen and I got our hands on Fenty Beauty’s new longwear foundation. When the brand launched in 2017, it was one of the first to offer a broad range of shades to match different skin tones. Now Fenty Beauty has reworked one of its original formulas with the release of the new pro filt’r fluid flex natural matte longwear foundation.

After eight years of development, customer feedback and testing, Fenty Beauty has attempted to make shade-matching more effective. It says the foundation doesn’t settle or crease in fine lines or pores, and is transfer-proof. Along with beauty expert Helen Wilson-Beevers, I put these claims to the test, reviewing the foundation’s staying power across several hours’ wear, to find out if it’s worth the hype.

Our favourite affordable homeware from Dusk

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

At IndyBest, we’ve come to know Dusk for its great-value furniture and homeware, having tested everything from its beds and sofas to its mattresses, dining furniture and more.

It’s one of the few home retailers at which you’ll find trend-led, affordable interiors, whether it’s armchairs starting from £100 or bed frames from £150. If it’s your first time shopping with Dusk, we’ve rounded up some of our favourite tried-and-tested products from the homeware brand to bring you a little inspiration for an interiors refresh.

Asian shares declined Friday tracking Wall Street losses, while oil prices gained with Brent crude trading above $108 a barrel in its highest since May.

U.S. futures edged higher.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8% to 63,442.30. Shares of multinational investment holding firm SoftBank Group, an investor of OpenAI, fell 4.1%.

South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3% to 6,872.39. Samsung Electronics slid 3.9%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix declined 3.6%.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8% to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8% to 3,862.73. Shares of Chinese AI chipmaker Enflame surged around 180% in its trading debut in Shanghai.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2% to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7%, while India’s Sensex declined 1%.

Oil prices continued to gain early Friday as tensions between the U.S. and Iran intensified. Brent crude, the international standard, was 0.9% higher at $108.59 per barrel. It was approximately $72 a barrel in late February, before the start of the war.

Benchmark U.S. crude was up 0.7% to $103.22 per barrel.

Oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway critical for global oil transport, remained “well below pre-war levels,” wrote ING commodities strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey in a commentary Friday. That’s “underscoring how fragile the situation has become,” they said.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6% in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7%.

Investors are also monitoring the U.S.’s consumer price index data for August set to be released Friday ahead of the Federal Reserve’s meeting next week.

Also on Thursday, the U.S. producer price index report for August was up 5.4% year-on-year, accelerating from July’s 4.8%.

The bond market has been volatile with U.S. Treasury yields well above pre-war levels, fueled by higher energy prices and inflationary pressures as well as rising U.S. government debt.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.96% early Friday from 4.83% on Wednesday.

In other dealings, the U.S. dollar fell to 154.35 Japanese yen from 154.42 yen. The euro was trading at $1.1605, down from $1.1612.

___

AP Business Writers Stan Choe and Anne D’Innocenzio contributed to this report.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Rampant Manchester United win first Champions League game in 1,003 days
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

News.title: ‘At that price, I’d expect it to make me a cup of tea’: Your verdict on Apple’s £2k foldable iPhone
News.content:
Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, was unveiled this week. With a starting price of £1999, it’s £300 more expensive than Samsung’s rival Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Similar in size to a British passport, when closed it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone. Once opened, it resembles a small iPad, allowing the user to open multiple apps at once.

News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

News.title: Britain pioneers new dried blood products for the modern battlefield
News.content:
A powdered blood product that can be mixed with water and used in minutes could help solve the challenges of treating severely wounded soldiers on hard-to-reach battlefields.

Britain is rethinking how to get blood to soldiers on the frontline, in the latest sign that the war in Ukraine has forced Western militaries to reconsider assumptions about modern combat medicine that had held since Iraq and Afghanistan.

The product, known as “spray-dried plasma”, is made by turning liquid plasma – the clotting-rich component of blood – into a stable powder that can be stored at room temperature for years before being rehydrated with water when needed.

“Plasma is vital for saving soldiers in war zones,” said Dr Ian Nesbitt, a former military anaesthetist and Faculty Lead for Anaesthesia at the David Nott Foundation, which trains doctors working in conflict zones.

“It helps blood clot when someone is injured. But in war zones, getting plasma to soldiers is incredibly complicated. It’s actually the logistics of it that are a real problem in maintaining a reliable supply of fresh frozen plasma for acutely injured patients.”

The NHS and the UK Ministry of Defence signed a strategic partnership this summer to jointly develop new blood products for frontline soldiers, focusing on dried plasma.

The agreement formalises work under way with a biotechnology company called Velico Medical. If successful, it will be used in future battlefields like the one in Ukraine.

“The war in Ukraine has woken up all countries, not just the UK,” Professor Renata Gomes, Chief Scientific Officer at NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT), told The Telegraph.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola issue called out as transfer chief breaks silence on star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola issue called out as transfer chief breaks silence on star

Bradley Barcola's first start for Liverpool has been addressed after a mixed evening in the Champions League for the former PSG winger

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola was criticised in some quarters for his performance on Wednesday night (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Liverpool face Fulham on Saturday, looking to uphold their recent good form. A comprehensive 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town last week was followed by a 2-1 Champions League win over Atletico Madrid on Wednesday, as the Reds got their European campaign underway.

‌



Andoni Iraola impressed during his first-ever game in Europe's premier competition as his side came from a goal down to secure the three points. Two talking points from the Champions League fixture have been the performances of new signing Bradley Barcola and Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo.

‌



The duo had somewhat contrasting evenings, with the ex-PSG man coming in for some criticism. Araujo, however, continues to shine in a relatively unfamiliar right-back role and his future has been discussed by a Barca transfer chief. Here, Mirror Football takes a closer look.

‌



Bradley Barcola issue called out

Barcola has been called out for his subpar finishing in the win over Atletico. The winger completed his £123million move from PSG late in August, with the two-time Champions League winner viewed as a game-changer for the Reds.

The left-sided forward made his debut off the bench in Friday's win at Ipswich but made his first start against Atleti on the right wing. Barcola lasted an hour before he was hooked with cramp but should've marked his maiden start with a goal.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Bayern Munich chief comes clean on Bradley Barcola transfer with Luis Diaz dig at Liverpool READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher sticks to his guns on Alexis Mac Allister after Liverpool contract dig READ MORE :

He saw an effort saved by Jan Oblak while he also fluffed a one-on-one, sending it wide of the post. Former Spurs star Tim Sherwood has taken Barcola to task for his underwhelming display in front of goal.

He said on Sky Sports: “No, it wasn’t a good night. He had a lot of opportunities. He looked a threat, but he had a few opportunities bearing down Oblak and he just couldn’t find the finish. He’s not a fantastic finisher, I have to say that. A few sitters he missed tonight.

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola started on the right wing for Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



“The good thing about him is that he stretches defenders. He runs without the ball, so you don’t have to take possession of the ball and dribble. He goes, checks and makes good runs.”

Iraola, however, is happy with the Reds' mega-money signing. He said: "I'm very happy because also he has had two very clear chances against the 'keeper. He hasn't scored, but I want him there."

Update on Araujo's future

Barcelona sporting director Deco offered a cryptic response about Araujo's long-term future. The Reds signed the 27-year-old on loan from the Catalan giants last month and have a £47m option to buy him permanently.

‌



Araujo has featured in all four of Liverpool’s games so far this season and has excelled at centre-back and while deputising at right-back. He has even shown attacking prowess, assisting Dominik Szoboszlai’s equaliser in the victory against Atleti.

View 4 Images Ronald Araujo has impressed so far (Image: 2026 Allstar)

Araujo's Barca exit was sanctioned after falling down the pecking order following a difficult season last term. Deco has admitted he doesn't know whether the defender will return to the Camp Nou, but has confessed he is a huge fan of the 27-year-old.

‌



“Yesterday I was watching the match of Liverpool,” Deco told RAC 1. “Good assist he made, huh? I was watching the match at home.

"I think football goes beyond just being a player of ours, right? I mean, to Ronald, I have affection for him, I love him, I want things to go well for him, I want him to succeed and be happy as a person.

View 4 Images Barcelona sporting director Deco has spoken about Araujo's loan move (Image: 2025 UEFA)

‌



“To me personally, he's a player that I love. For me, at some moment he couldn't be at his best moment, but I think Ronald has been, until now, his spell at Barca has been spectacular. Sometimes ideas don't coincide, the player's moment, and sometimes it's good to look for an exit, that also helps you.

“I don't know [if he’ll come back], let's see, he has a contract with us. It's very early still. He's a player that we have a lot of respect for and I would tell you plenty of affection, not only us as a club, but also the locker room, so from here, let's see. It's a topic for the future."

Meanwhile, the Uruguayan has claimed that he is happy at Anfield. “Liverpool is a big club like Barcelona,” he told Movistar. “You have to give your best and there are high expectations. I am happy, I’m working hard as you can see also on the pitch. I am happy here and hungry for more."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Michael Carrick makes rule change as club's Premier League request granted
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick makes rule change as club's Premier League request granted

Manchester United are preparing for a huge game in the Premier League and Michael Carrick is also focused on the club's long-term future

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has overseen a key change at Manchester United (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Manchester United are facing an important weekend in the Premier League but have also begun planning for the future. Michael Carrick’s side are preparing to take on rivals Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday.

‌



The Red Devils are looking to return to winning ways in the league following their dramatic draw with Everton last weekend. The United boss has many options at his disposal, but could also look to the club’s academy to bolster his matchday squad.

‌



Carrick has kept a close eye on the academy sides since returning to United at the start of the year. JJ Gabriel was among the youngsters to feature for the first team during pre-season, and a rule change during the manager's reign is set to benefit the academy hopefuls looking to make the step up.

‌



Meanwhile, the Premier League have granted United’s request regarding their upcoming schedule. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the team.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Michael Carrick makes rule change

United’s academy starlets have received a boost to their dreams of reaching the first team, with the club’s U21 side replicating Carrick’s system. Under the new approach, U21 coach Adam Lawrence has changed from a 4-3-3 to a 4-2-3-1 formation.

‌



The policy being introduced during Carrick's tenure will grant all academy hopefuls a smoother step up to the first team as players will be familiar with the demands of their role. The Daily Mail reports that the team have also copied Carrick’s deployment of a false nine, mirroring the manager’s use of Matheus Cunha.

It is hinted that Chido Obi being loaned out and academy forward Louie Bradbury leaving for Stoke City could signal a long-term move away from orthodox strikers. Meanwhile, the formation switch will allow 15-year-old prodigy Gabriel to learn Bruno Fernandes’ position as he establishes himself in the U21 side.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is among United's top academy prospects (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Premier League request granted

The Premier League have responded to requests from United and other clubs by agreeing to announce their festive schedule. The Red Devils pushed for the league and broadcasters to make an earlier decision on which games would be televised in December to allow supporters more time to plan.

The Daily Mail reports that United met with senior Premier League and broadcast officials to request that the information be published more than a month earlier than last year. The announcement that the club would host Newcastle on Boxing Day in 2025 was made on October 31.

Article continues below

It is added that the Football Supporters Association were involved in talks over bringing the announcement forward to help fans plan their journeys. All fixtures were originally listed as 3pm kick-offs on Saturday, December 26 but were subject to change.

It has been confirmed that United will host Nottingham Forest on Sunday, December 27, with a 4.30pm kick-off. The team will also play Sunderland under the floodlights at Old Trafford in a 7.30pm game on Wednesday, December 30.

Sports.title: Premier League stars obsessed with collecting football cards in their free time
Sports.content:
Premier League stars obsessed with collecting football cards in their free time

Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton sold his Topps card collection earlier this year for over £2,000 to YouTuber Jack White

View 3 Images Adam Wharton with YouTuber Jack White (GBW)

Premier League players are taking their obsession for the sport to the next level - by collecting football cards.

‌



In their downtime away from playing and training, big names such as Declan Rice, Dominic Solanke and Tosin Adarabioyo were seen either opening or promoting cards or collectibles. Many footballers even have their own separate trading card Instagram accounts.

‌



One of them is Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton, who recently sold his Topps card collection for over £2,000 to YouTuber Jack White. Jack, 26, who runs the GBW account and is from Kent, has been collecting stickers or cards for the last 20 years and now has over 200,000 YouTube subscribers and over 100,000 followers on Tiktok.

‌



He said: "I started collecting while in primary school aged 5/6 and then that progressed into Match Attax from the very first collection. I started filming myself open packs when I was 12 while at secondary school, so been going ever since."

3 View 3 Images Jack's favourite is the Messi Argentina 100 club 101 card 3 View 3 Images Jack says the 1/1 Autographed Clive Tyldesley is his most valuable

‌



When asked which of his prized cards is his favourite, Jack said: "My most valuable would be the 1/1 autographed Clive Tyldesley from Topps UCC Decades 90s Edition which came out in 2025. But my favourite is the Messi Argentina 100 club 101 card which graded a PSA 8 and is one for the collection forever. It's topical too now with his recent retirement."

Jack is not only a massive collector but he's also one of the UK's top content creators for card collectibles. He was keen to offer footy mad youngsters tips on getting into the profession. He said: "My best advice would be to block out the outside noise. Because when I started I had people telling me to stop because cards were deemed ‘not cool’ back then.

"Focus on showing off your passion and an audience will follow. People watch and like GBW because of the longevity perhaps, I’ve got a good personality on camera which I think shines through, not sure! That’s one for my audience to tell me. But this hobby is massive now because of the likes of Match Attax and now new hobby sets with big names starting to collect like the sidemen."

‌



Benjamin Hobart, the Managing Director of SideCards, said: "Over the past few years, we've seen more and more footballers publicly show their interest in collecting. Players like Eden Hazard have been very open about collecting with their children, while Declan Rice has filmed pack-opening videos with members of the Sidemen. Then you have the next generation coming through, with players like JJ Gabriel joining us for a break to celebrate the launch of his first-ever set, Topps Flagship, earlier this year.

"At SideCards, we have personally been lucky to break products with some of the biggest names in the sporting world and, more often than not, once they start ripping packs, it's pretty hard to get them to stop! They get exactly the same buzz we all do from opening a product and hunting for the big chase cards, especially when they're actually in the set themselves."

Lewis Hamilton has recently ventured into the hobby in a commercial capacity, opening his first store in Frankfurt, Germany. Benjamin added: "While seeing players embrace the hobby so publicly still feels relatively new in the UK, the relationship between professional athletes and collectables is already far more established in the US. It feels like athletes in the UK are now starting to follow the same path, with the players themselves becoming collectors, fans of the hobby and, ultimately, an important part of its continued growth."

Article continues below

Match Attax, the UK's original football trading card game, turns 20 this year. Created to celebrate two decades of collecting, swapping and playing, the 20th Anniversary Edition brings a host of serious upgrades for the 2026/27 season. The biggest change comes with an all-new rarity system, with new symbols helping collectors identify cards from Rare, Super-Rare, Mega-Rare, Ultra-Rare, Hyper-Rare through to the ultimate Mystical full-art cards.

Sports.title: West Ham star threatens legal action over 'false allegations' after kidnap claims
Sports.content:
West Ham star threatens legal action over 'false allegations' after kidnap claims

West Ham United player Edson Alvarez is the subject of kidnapping claims, which he denies, and he is now threatening legal action over these 'false allegations'

View 2 Images Edson Alvarez has played just once for West Ham United this season (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

West Ham United player Edson Alvarez has broken his silence over allegations linking him to a kidnapping. The Mexico captain categorically rejects the claims and is threatening legal action against what he describes as false allegations.

‌



Alvarez, 28, is being connected to the alleged kidnapping of Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez, who claims to have produced a documentary about the player's career on his behalf. It is said to have cost over £150,000 (3.5 million pesos), which is apparently still outstanding.

‌



The producer has spoken to Mexican entertainment magazine TVNotas. Ordonez claims he was kidnapped two years ago after demanding payment.

‌



Baffled Champions League star learns his manager resigned straight after final whistle READ MORE :

Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision READ MORE :

In an obscure statement posted in both English and Spanish on his Instagram account, Alvarez says: "In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly. I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.

"Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

"Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line.

‌



View 2 Images Edson Alvarez captained Mexico at the World Cup (Image: Jam Media, Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it. Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritises sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth.

‌



"I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure. Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me.

"I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner's father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported.

Sports.title: Man Utd star JJ Gabriel sparks social media concern after record-breaking hat-trick
Sports.content:
Man Utd star JJ Gabriel sparks social media concern after record-breaking hat-trick

Young Man Utd star JJ Gabriel has drawn plenty of attention for his displays in the club's academy teams and fans will be eager to see him in the first team

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is one of Man Utd's brightest prospects (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel has wiped all images from his Instagram profile. The striker bagged a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut during Thursday's 5-0 thrashing of Sabah FK Under-19s.

‌



Gabriel found the net in the 45th, 85th and 87th minutes to cement his reputation as one of the Red Devils' most promising prospects. He became the youngest-ever player to net a treble for United in the European competition, aged just 15 years and 339 days.

‌



The rising talent has captured supporters' imaginations, generating considerable buzz at Old Trafford. However, the teenager has curiously deleted every photograph from his Instagram account, apparently without offering any reason.

‌



Man Utd batter Sabah to enjoy dream Champions League return - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd receive explanation from Barcelona for Marcus Rashford transfer snub READ MORE :

Speculation is rife over whether he might break into Michael Carrick's first-team squad for Premier League action this season.

Top-flight rules in English football stipulate that a player must reach 15 on or before August 31 of a particular season to qualify for league selection. This meant he was ineligible to appear in the last campaign, but could now feature in 2026/27.

Should Reds boss Carrick give him an outing before he turns 16 in October, the youngster would become United's youngest-ever first-team player. The Reds' academy players have been given a boost in their bid to break into the first team, with U21 boss Adam Lawrence switching from a 4-3-3 formation to mirror Carrick's 4-2-3-1 system.

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel featured for Manchester United during pre-season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

The tactical shift should mean United's youngsters, Gabriel included, arrive in the senior setup with a far clearer grasp of what is expected of them.

The formation change is said to give Gabriel the opportunity to get to grips with Bruno Fernandes' No. 10 role.

‌



Meanwhile, the U21s have replicated Carrick's use of Matheus Cunha as a false nine by deploying Amir Ibragimov in the striker's position.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko sends clear message to Michael Carrick on night of few revelations for Man Utd
Sports.content:
Benjamin Sesko sends clear message to Michael Carrick on night of few revelations for Man Utd

Manchester United made light work for Azerbaijani side Sabah on their return to the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko sending a reminder to Michael Carrick with a well-taken goal

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko took his goal well (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

When Benjamin Sesko was sent clear by Byran Mbeumo’s pass just before half-time, it never crossed his mind to fall under the rash challenge of goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov.

‌



He took the contact, did all he could to stay upright and rewarded himself with a routine finish. It is what natural-born central strikers do.

‌



From a formality of a night against hapless opponents, Michael Carrick learnt little of significance. But he was reminded that Sesko is a line-leader, an identikit number nine, even though he does not have it on his back.

‌



The Slovenian attacker has yet to start a Premier League match this season but will surely become the regular spearhead of this attack. And not just on the evidence of a good game against a team that will give target practice to everyone they meet in this phase of the Champions League.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Sesko scored a classic centre-forward’s goal when he came on as a late substitute and has been clinical for this United side since Carrick took over. And every angry-looking celebration tells you that he believes he should be starting every game.

It will be interesting to see if Carrick goes with him against Manchester City. And as soon as Sesko had hit United’s third of the night, the manager’s thoughts must have drifted towards Sunday’s challenge against Manchester City. Because this turned out to be as easy a task as everyone expected.

The nature of the game - a comfortable 4-0 win - gave Carrick the chance to try a new defensive combination but different personnel did not completely erase familiar failings.

‌



View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko waltzed around the Sabah goalkeeper to score (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

The failings were never going to be costly against an extremely limited attacking unit but there was still a distinct lack of assurance on the rare occasions the champions of Azerbaijan threatened to cause an offensive problem.

You would certainly expect to see Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot return to the starting line-up for the Manchester derby. And if he is fit, Luke Shaw - allowed to have a night off after what must have been a particularly severe case of cramp against Everton - will probably return to the side.

‌



In attacking mode, Patrick Dorgu was decent - setting up the opening goal for Matheus Cunha - but defensively, he was not convincing. He was exposed a couple of times, not least when Joy-Lance Mickels somehow failed to head home a sitter that would have levelled the score.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick rotated his team for the Sabah game (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Predictably, regret for Mickels and Sabah arrived fairly instantly, Bruno Fernandes applying side-footed justice to a nice Youri Tielemans assist. And after Sesko’s copybook finish, any pretence that it could be a meaningful contest had to be shelved.

‌



It was then just a case of how ruthless United would be in the second half. Sesko was withdrawn just after the hour mark - which might augur well for his chances of making Sunday's starting line-up - and it was over to Joshua Zirkzee to have a crack up top. And Zirkzee was involved in a comedy fourth for United that was eventually claimed by Lisandro Martinez.

That was the signal for Carrick to give an outing to youngsters Harry Amass and Shea Lacey and they enjoyed a nice 20 minutes in the Champions League limelight.

It was a pleasant end to a pleasant, if bloodless, return to the grand European stage.

Sports.title: Man Utd batter Sabah to enjoy dream Champions League return - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Man Utd batter Sabah to enjoy dream Champions League return - 5 talking points

MANCHESTER UNITED 4-0 SABAH: Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko and Lisandro Martinez saw Michael Carrick chalk up his first win in the Champions League as full-time United boss

View 3 Images Youri Tielemans teed Bruno Fernandes up for Man United's second goal (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United ended their near three-year exile from the Champions League in style with a 4-0 win against Sabah.

‌



The Red Devils took the lead midway through the first half as Matheus Cunha converted from Patrick Dorgu's cross. Sabah went close to equalising soon after as Joy-Lance Mickels nodded wide from close range.

‌



But the home side took full control before the break with goals from Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko. Michael Carrick opted for changes during the second-half, with the Manchester Derby on the horizon this weekend.

‌



There was still time for Lisandro Martinez to round off the route. Here are all of the talking points from Old Trafford.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Dorgu proves a point

After Man United's issues at left back, boss Carrick was forced into some thinking against Sabah. And the solution he stumbled upon was deploying Dorgu in the position.

There were a few uncomfortable moments, notably a handball that went unpunished in the first half. But he performed well all things considered.

As always, his attacking pedigree was his strongest asset, the Dane being on hand to play a perfect pass to Cunha for the Red Devils' opener.

‌



Dorgu eventually came off for Harry Amass, who was handed a brief cameo by Carrick.

View 3 Images Patrick Dorgu played in a slightly unfamiliar position against Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Cunha responds to axe

Across the Man United side, Brazilian forward Cunha was arguably one of the most experienced from a Champions League perspective. Ahead of the clash with Sabah, he had made 12 appearances in the competition, albeit the one thing that was missing was a goal.

‌



Considered unlucky for some, his first goal came on his 13th outing as he converted from Dorgu's low cross.

It was a relatively simple finish but it's one that will be a relief for the forward. He will also feel as though he has responded in the best possible way to Carlo Ancelotti's decision to leave him out of his most recent Brazil squad.

Fernandes on fire

After a hat-trick on his last appearances at Old Trafford vs Ipswich, Fernandes was at it again against Sabah. And it was another brilliant move from Carrick's side.

‌



Each of Dorgu, Cunha and Youri Tielemans got on the ball, with the Belgian playing a lovely ball to Fernandes, who finished first time with his right foot.

He now has four goals in as many games this season, as well as an assist. The Portuguese playmaker deserves to be on the Champions League stage - and it's a delight to see him back.

View 3 Images Fernandes and Sesko were both on the scoresheet vs Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sesko in the goals again

After seeing the joy of a late winner against Everton stripped away from him last time out, Sesko will have been keen to get on the scoresheet once again - particularly after being named in the starting line-up for the first time this season.

And he did just that after getting on the end of a brilliant pass from Mbeumo, skipping around the goalkeeper and finishing into an empty net.

His build-up play and passing still need work but after just 12 goals last season, the Slovenian forward will be happy with his hot start to this campaign.

‌



Messy from Sabah

Joshua Zirkzee has not had the best time of things since joining Manchester United. The Dutchman appeared to be on the way out of Old Trafford in January.

And he might have been cursing his luck against Sabah. After being introduced as a substitute, the Dutchman attempted to score with an audacious backheel.

His effort was deflected away but bounced off of the defender and the goalkeeper, before falling at the feet of Martinez, who lashed home. It was an extremely bizarre and messy goal but Martinez will not care, while Zirkzee looked away in slight disgust that he didn't find the net.

Sports.title: UFC star Paddy Pimblett admits he wants to ‘beat up’ Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta as challenge laid out
Sports.content:
UFC star Paddy Pimblett admits he wants to ‘beat up’ Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta as challenge laid out

Paddy Pimblett has been a vocal critic of Arsenal and their manager Mikel Arteta in recent years, and the UFC fighter has now gone one step further

View 2 Images UFC star Paddy Pimblett has pulled no punches (Image: Getty Images)

UFC fighter and Liverpool supporter Paddy Pimblett has jokingly declared he would love to get in the ring with Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. The Huyton-born brawler has made no secret of his disdain for the Gunners and their boss.

‌



The 31-year-old revealed last season that he had been rooting for Manchester City to deny Arteta's side Premier League glory, with both clubs locked in a gripping title race full of dramatic twists and turns.

‌



Yet it was Arsenal who ultimately triumphed — clinching their first league title in 22 years. That success saw the north Londoners finish the 2025/26 campaign seven points clear of their rivals, ending a run of agonising near-misses in previous seasons.

‌



Martin Odegaard has changed his approach and is transforming Arsenal for the better READ MORE :

Bayern Munich chief comes clean on Bradley Barcola transfer with Luis Diaz dig at Liverpool READ MORE :

The Gunners are among the favourites to defend their crown this term and have made a flying start, winning all three of their opening fixtures. But Pimblett is firmly not among those singing their praises.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When quizzed by host Jamie Theakston on Thursday's Heart UK breakfast show about who he would most want to fight, he said: "At the minute I'd probably say Mikel Arteta just to beat him up."

‌



Pimblett's remarks came after he had previously laid into Arteta's side ahead of their title win in May, taking aim at the club's fanbase during an appearance on The Wayne Rooney Show.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is not on Paddy Pimblett's Christmas list (Image: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"Come on City, come on City," he cried. "I want them to win, you know what I mean? I hate Arsenal fans.
