He cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer who was dismissed after criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay
Sports.content:
The Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job.

Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.

Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure,” he said. Asked whether the manager had told him he would stay, Yildirim said: “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family.”

Kartal, who spent a decade at Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis in 2021-22 before returning for a full ⁠campaign in 2023-24. He was the assistant manager at Fenerbahce the ​past two ​times the club won ​the Turkish title, and returned for a fourth ​managerial spell in ‌June.

View image in fullscreen Archie Brown celebrates his equaliser for Fenerbahce. The English full-back was left dumbfounded when learning of his coach’s resignation after the final whistle. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Fenerbahce have ​finished second ​in the Turkish Super Lig in each of the past five seasons, and reached the Champions League’s league phase this season for the first time in 18 years. The team sit ninth in the Turkish top-flight, having lost twice in their opening four games, including Saturday’s 2-1 home defeat to Besiktas.

Roma took the lead in the 39th minute when Donyell Malen rolled a pass to ​Bryan Cristante, who beat Fenerbahce keeper Ederson with a bouncing finish. The hosts levelled before half-time when Mason Greenwood slipped a ​pass through to Archie ​Brown, who clipped a finish over ​Mile Svilar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Roma were awarded a penalty in the 68th minute when ​Kerem Akturkoglu was ‌penalised for a ​foul on Paulo ​Dybala, but a VAR check ruled that the challenge had taken place outside the area. Fenerbahce came closest to grabbing a winner late on when Nathan Aké headed against the Roma crossbar.

Fenerbahce will travel to Aston Villa and host Liverpool in two of their remaining league phase games – whether Kartal will be in charge or not remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino: ‘I am always open to help Tottenham. In whatever division’
Sports.content:
If things had worked out differently, Mauricio Pochettino would have gone back to his beloved Tottenham over the summer. They had put in the call and it stirred him. Nothing was going to put him off – not even the possibility of the club being in the Championship.

Seriously, Mauricio? After a World Cup campaign with the United States and top jobs with Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain before that, he would have been willing to start a new chapter in the second tier of English football? “Yes, of course,” Pochettino says. “Tottenham … it’s the only club that always I am open to help. In whatever division.”

Football is about timing and Pochettino was left to reflect on how his stars did not align. It has been a theme of his managerial career, along with the desire to keep an eye out for greener pastures. And not be shy about doing so.

Spurs’ idea after sacking Thomas Frank in February was to get to the end of the season under the interim Igor Tudor, when they could assess a potentially deeper pool of candidates. They knew that if Pochettino was to be their man, they would have to wait for him because he was contracted to the US until after the World Cup. There was no way he could walk out on that challenge. Nor would he have wanted to.

Then the picture changed. When Tudor bombed, leaving Spurs one point above the relegation zone with seven games to play, they pivoted to Roberto De Zerbi, who said no to them after they dismissed Frank. De Zerbi had just left Marseille and needed a break. Now Spurs made him a long-term offer he could not refuse. And so Pochettino felt the door close to the club where he managed for five-and-a-half years from 2014; where he established such a strong connection.

“The problem was that the timings were never the best,” he says. “When I was free, I never received a contact and then when I was working, I received a contact but I cannot make the decision to come back. It was a little bit unlucky. Maybe one day the stars will align and it can happen. If I was free, of course, I come. But I wasn’t free. I was preparing the World Cup.”

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino, celebrating after the dramatic semi-final win against Ajax, led Tottenham to the Champions League final in 2019. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Was the door to Spurs ever truly open for Pochettino? The club have insisted that De Zerbi was their No 1 target for the summer before they were forced to move ahead of time. Perhaps we will never know. But one thing is clear: these kind of teasers and Pochettino’s openness about them are a part of his story. They add to his swaggering appeal. In a game where micromanaged content is the norm, where managers are tied in knots by the party line, there is something exhilarating about hearing Pochettino hold court.

The 54-year-old has always had his suitors, ever since he first began to establish his reputation as a forward-thinking coach and charismatic man-manager at Espanyol, where he took charge in 2009. He has always liked to keep them close and he always will do. Should US Soccer be worried? Pochettino has just signed a new four-year contract to take him up to the 2030 World Cup. That is probably an unhealthy way of thinking. Better for the federation to focus on how it has one of the game’s elite managers and accept that they will have options.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino has signed a new deal with the United States that will take him through to the 2030 World Cup. Photograph: Todd Kirkland/FIFA/Getty Images

Pochettino has had his share of sliding-doors moments. He was linked to the Real Madrid job in November 2017 as Zinedine Zidane was tipped for the sack only for the Frenchman to hang on and end up winning the Champions League that season. Two days before the final against Liverpool, Pochettino signed a new long-term contract at Spurs. Five days after it, Zidane announced his shock resignation. It was not the first or, indeed, the last time that Pochettino was linked to Madrid.

There have been links with Manchester United. The club considered him when they sacked Louis van Gaal in 2016, when they dismissed José Mourinho in 2018 and turned to Ole Gunnar Solskjær, initially on an interim basis (Solskjær would make the job his own), and before they hired Erik ten Hag in 2022.

Then there was England. Pochettino was in the conversation as the Football Association looked for a successor to Sir Gareth Southgate after Euro 2024. The way Pochettino tells it, he committed to the US in August of that year and it was before the FA started its search in earnest. It would end with it choosing Thomas Tuchel.

Would Pochettino consider the England job one day? He is aware that his Argentinian nationality would present an issue – because of the Falklands conflict and the history between the countries on the football pitch. It was fractious when they clashed in the World Cup semi-final in July, Argentina winning 2-1. But Pochettino does not see it as a deal-breaker.

“Maybe, yes,” he says of coaching England. “If you consider in a few years’ time, yes … if I got an approach. One thing I don’t want because the USA guys will kill me is if you say the headline is: ‘Mauricio will consider English job.’ It is like I am considering it now. No. Not now. If I am free [in the future].

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino, still adored by Tottenham fans, says the north London team is ‘still my club’. Photograph: Tony O’Brien/Action Images/Reuters

“My respect is that it’s football. I am the first to feel for my people in Argentina but at the end of the day it’s just football. The World Cup semi-final was just one game of football, although people wanted to convert it to other subjects. It is true that it can be controversial because an Argentinian guy is thinking to maybe one day defend the flag of England and we were involved in a war …”

Pochettino still has his family home in north London. He has a love affair with the city and England. “We are very similar, Argentinian and English people, in the way we feel the passion of football,” he says. “I love the countryside here, too. I think you respect all the things that I also grew up with in my country.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In Argentina, I lived in a town in Murphy with a lot of Irish and British people around. And all the clubs … Racing Club, River Plate, Newell’s Old Boys. They are English language names, no? Now I am here doing my passion that is football and I cannot work here [for England]? Why? It is crazy. I really believe in the diplomatic things, going to talk and for sure to find the best way.”

Pochettino extended his contract with the US for many reasons, among them the faith the federation had shown in him. They offered him the four-year deal before the World Cup kicked off, which he appreciated greatly. He signed it in August. The challenge excites him – to change the perception of the game in the country, to build something. He has made a good start.

The World Cup ended badly with the 4-1 defeat by Belgium in the last 16. The game was overshadowed by the Folarin Balogun controversy; how the US federation was able to overturn the striker’s suspension amid trademark grandstanding from Donald Trump. It ought to have been a blessing. It ended up as a curse, affecting Balogun and the team; giving Belgium even more of a cause. But before that, everything had gone extremely well.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino managed USA to the last-16 of this summer’s World Cup. Photograph: Alex Livesey/FIFA/Getty Images

The free-flowing 4-1 victory against Paraguay in the opening game sparked a feelgood factor. Then came the comfortable win over Australia to secure qualification from the group with a game to spare. Bosnia and Herzegovina were swatted aside in the last 32. “We created something,” Pochettino says. “The fans were amazing. We never expected the fans in this way. The players changed completely the mindset.”

Pochettino’s situation, though, does feel different with the longer contract – certainly to him. “Now it is a different thing,” he says. “When we gave our word to the federation [in August 2024], it was about starting and finishing after the World Cup. For us, it was the moment to say: ‘If some club comes, it’s impossible.’ Always you can break a contract, say you stop and that’s it … you agree something. But in the moment it wasn’t right for us to create all these situations and expectations.

“Now it’s a four-year contract, it’s different. We can next season lose the Copa América or the Gold Cup, they’re not happy with us and they can sack us. Or we can say: ‘OK. It’s not in the way that we think.’ Four years is different. Maybe now if someone calls in the future, it’s a different, different type [of thing]. We are excited, we are thinking to spend four years to the next World Cup. But now it’s a long period.”

The conversation turns back to Spurs. As it often does with Pochettino. He says his former striker Harry Kane, who is at Bayern Munich, would be a deserving winner of this year’s Ballon d’Or. He insists he was pleased to see De Zerbi get more than £300m to spend on players over the summer; a figure he could only have dreamed about. “I am happy because I feel Tottenham … it’s still my club,” Pochettino says. And there is another window into his soul when he reflects on how Spurs got rid of the longstanding chair, Daniel Levy, last September – the man who dismissed him.

“I think he feels like I did when I was sacked,” Pochettino says. “I keep in touch with him and I never made the situation personal because you can sack a coach. The way I felt in that moment … you receive the letter, you pick up your things and you can never come back to say goodbye to the people, maybe 200, 300 people, that were your family. You cannot send a text, you cannot do nothing.

“That was really, really tough for me and I was talking with him [Levy] about that. Of course, I am not happy that now he feels the same because I am not a person who has bad feelings. But yes, it’s difficult for him and his family and I am so sorry for him.”

Pochettino is ready for the next phase of his US adventure. As ever, his mind and heart race with possibility.

Sports.title: Declan Rice shrugs off Arsenal concerns and says 60 games a season is sustainable
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has insisted his body can sustain more than 60 appearances again this season, despite Arsenal’s concerns after he played through pain at the World Cup.

Rice racked up 69 appearances last season for Arsenal and England but revealed during the World Cup he had been managing neural back and hamstring pain, for which he is understood to have received a pain-killing injection, after a hamstring injury in December. It is understood Arsenal are monitoring the 27-year-old’s workload closely after he had only three weeks off before returning to training a week before the Community Shield last month.

Rice came off the bench to replace Bruno Guimarães in the victory over Manchester City in Cardiff and has since started all Arsenal’s matches, with Guimarães’ return from an injury being managed. A major reason why Arsenal bought the Brazil midfielder for £75m from Newcastle was to take some strain off from Rice, although it was noticeable that Rice played all of Wednesday’s Champions League victory at Napoli, with Mikel Merino coming off for Guimarães.

“I think for the last six seasons, even since my West Ham days when they were in Europe, I’ve played 60-plus every season,” Rice said. “So I think it is sustainable because I’ve shown that I can do it.

“It’s just about maintaining it, maintaining the level and the consistency of the performances. For me, that’s the main thing, showing up every week, giving a good account of myself and helping the team win. I’ve been lucky enough to be able to do that. So I’m really hungry to be able to do that again this season.”

It is understood Arsenal offered Rice more time off after the World Cup exploits but that he was keen to return for the start of the season. He is expected to be part of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia when it is announced next Friday, although whether he features in all four matches remains to be seen, with Arsenal likely to request that he and Bukayo Saka are given another opportunity to rest. Rice said he had found things “tough” during the World Cup but is adamant he is feeling “refreshed”.

“I feel really good at the minute, in really good form, so we’ll make it continue,” he said. “I think everyone knew I had an issue with a neural hamstring. But also on the top of the Premier League season, which was so demanding, the Champions League, to then play a World Cup in that heat really does take its toll. I’m a player that goes on the pitch, wants to be fresh and give 100% every time I put on an England shirt. Yes, there were stages where I felt really, really good and stages where I didn’t feel so good. There were a few things that frustrated me, just with myself, just not feeling 100%. It’s one of those things I just had to manage.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Rice is one of three England players nominated for the Ballon d’Or this week, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane. The ceremony, traditionally in Paris, will take place in London on 26 October as a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the inaugural award in 1956, and Rice has backed Kane to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. “I would Iove to see Harry win it,” he said. “So I’m wishing him all the best in that.”

Sports.title: How Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard's inseparable bond is powering their resurgent form - trips abroad together, the running joke at Arsenal's HQ and how Gunners captain helped Havertz and his wife Sophia cope with vile abuse
Sports.content:
Footballing chemistry, fatherhood and wives that are best friends. All these elements, and more, have made Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard inseparable at Arsenal.

The Havertz and Odegaard show has taken centre stage at the club recently, their on-pitch performances powering the strongest of starts for the reigning Premier League champions.

In all competitions this term, Arsenal have struck ten goals, with the pair responsible for seven of them.

Havertz’s dummy fooled Chelsea's backline on Sunday – but not Odegaard, who strolled through to collect Christos Tzolis’ cross and score.

Most recently, Odegaard rescued a victory away at Napoli on Wednesday night in the Champions League after an impressive Gunners display wasn't matched by their finishing (their expected goals – or xG – exceeded four).

As Tzolis’ pass reached the Norwegian just outside the area, his eyes lit up, driving forward on that wand of a left foot.

Once he saw a gap, the captain curled the ball with pace and precision into the bottom-left corner to make it four goals in five matches for a man on a mission to prove he is worthy of a place at the top table of elite midfielders.

Martin Odegaard (left) and Kai Havertz have been two of the stars of Arsenal's impressive start to the 2026-27 season

The pair's goalscoring form has been helped by a close bond off the pitch, which is the subject of a running joke at Arsenal's HQ

The reigning Premier League champions have scored ten goals in all competitions this term, and Havertz and Odegaard struck seven of them

Odegaard and Havertz's recent performances have been helped by their bond off the pitch, the pair behaving more like brothers than colleagues.

After joining the Gunners from Chelsea for £65million in June 2023, Havertz initially endured a tough time in north London.

The left-sided midfield position Arteta had earmarked for the German was proving a mismatch, Havertz struggling to adapt to the role.

The nadir saw Havertz be the recipient of widespread groans at the Emirates during a 3-1 win over Manchester United in which he lost the ball in the build-up to Marcus Rashford's opener.

He wasn’t scoring, either, enduring a nine-game drought which ended against Bournemouth in September 2023, Odegaard having grabbed the ball to gift his team-mate the penalty.

Havertz rolled it home for his first Arsenal goal. The captain performed a similar gesture for Viktor Gyokeres against Everton last December, allowing the Swede to take a penalty amid a tricky goalscoring period for the striker.

Odegaard took it upon himself to help Havertz settle. A shy character, despite his imposing 6ft 4in frame, the German has benefitted from the support of his Norwegian team-mate.

Their wives, Helene Spilling and Sophia Weber, are close. The couples have holidayed together. Havertz was a groomsman at Odegaard's wedding.

They also became fathers just months apart, at the same age of 25. Odegaard and Helene announced in August 2024 that they were expecting a baby. Their son, Matheo, was born on December 1, 2024.

Havertz and Sophia made their announcement in November 2024, before Sophia gave birth in March 2025.

Odegaard and Havertz holidayed together in Ibiza during the off-season of 2024

The pair with their wives Helene Spilling and Sophia Weber, who are also firm friends

It’s a running joke around the club about how close the pair are. It reflects the qualities of a captain who is said to be the glue between his team.

When Sophia was subjected to horrific abuse on Instagram after Havertz had his penalty saved in an FA Cup defeat by Manchester United in January 2025 – which included threats against their unborn child – Odegaard stayed in close contact with Havertz, supporting the family through it.

Odegaard was the first player to text Havertz when he joined. He did the same for other players, too, like Gyokeres and Mikel Merino. From advice on the best areas to live and restaurant recommendations, to an open door whenever help is needed, he makes himself available.

He is also known to ring players who are going through a tough period to check in on them and offer his support.

Last season, even when he wasn't playing due to injury, the role Odegaard played behind the scenes was highly valued by Arteta and his staff.

He was said to be busy around the training ground and on matchdays, organising different elements. Team preferences on minor details like timings and rest were gathered by Odegaard and passed on to staff.

Another similarity – both Havertz and Odegaard faced their fair share of adversity last season and are now hellbent on making up for lost time.

Havertz suffered an knee injury on the opening day of the last campaign in August, which kept him out for five months, before sustaining a few muscle issues later in the season.

His captain, meanwhile, suffered a shoulder injury in September 2025, a knee issue in October and from March onwards.

Odegaard missed much of last season through injury, scoring just one goal in all competitions. This campaign he looks a man reborn

As does Havertz, who was kept out by a knee injury for five months from the beginning of 2025-26

Now the pair are determined to make up for lost time - and inspire Arsenal to more silverware

These issues derailed their campaigns. Odegaard, for example, scored just one goal in all competitions. That is how stark the drop-off was, and makes his recent form all the more impressive.

Both players have become central figures in Arteta’s Arsenal, and with both fit, confident and producing again, their understanding could prove decisive in the club’s pursuit of more silverware.

From holiday plans to difficult moments, the pair have built a relationship that stretches well beyond the pitch. Now, Havertz and Odegaard look determined to make up for lost time – together.

Sports.title: Why Man City are fired up to end their Old Trafford hoodoo: Squad unity, the star duo drumming standards into newcomers and the missing ingredient players say Enzo Maresca has added ahead of Man United clash
Sports.content:
Why Man City are fired up to end their Old Trafford hoodoo: Squad unity, the star duo drumming standards into newcomers and the missing ingredient players say Enzo Maresca has added ahead of Man United clash

Ayyoub Bouaddi has done his homework. He looks a little bit bookish, so that stands to reason.

Aside from naming no fewer than four Manchester City midfielders – Messrs Toure, De Bruyne, Gundogan and Rodri – when asked for a Premier League idol growing up, the 18-year-old born just north of Paris studiously learned his lines on this weekend’s derby.

‘The most important game of the year,’ Bouaddi said softly but deliberately. ‘It means a lot for the fans and for us. We will give everything for this game.’

Watching the togetherness of City’s squad in recent weeks, particularly in Porto’s white-hot cauldron of aggravation on Tuesday, it feels like a hop across town to Manchester United is exactly what they crave. To roll on to the next big event, riding a wave.

Erling Haaland and Gianluigi Donnarumma, two deputies of captain Ruben Dias, are said to be drumming in the standards of the club to the new signings in the hope they can integrate quickly. Haaland is becoming more vocal and has started this season boisterously.

And listening to Bouaddi, the recent recruits have clearly taken heed.

Erling Haaland celebrates his second goal in Man City's 2-0 win over Porto. The Norwegian has become noticeably more vocal this season

City's Ayyoub Bouaddi already knows the importance of Sunday's derby. 'It means a lot for the fans and for us,' he said. 'We will give everything for this game’

Sunday's derby probably comes a touch too soon in the reign of Enzo Maresca to draw any real conclusions on the ultimate direction of the team this season but it is an opportunity to lay down a marker that the status quo up here is not changing just because the messiah took his leave into the Catalonian sunset.

In fact, there is definitely something for the Italian to improve upon – and it is not often we will be able to say that when comparing to the Guardiola era. The record at Old Trafford is patchy at best.

Of the stadiums that City have visited more than once over the last seven campaigns, they’ve only fared worse at Tottenham. It’s an average of a point a game in north London – four defeats, two wins, one draw.

Only marginally better is the 1.14 points-per-game at United. Exactly the same number as Anfield, even though the fortunes of those two clubs have been worlds apart.

Two wins, two draws and three defeats since 2019 simply does not tally with City’s supremacy over their crosstown rivals. They haven’t scored a goal there since 2023, were wretched amid a defensive injury crisis in January – Michael Carrick’s first game in caretaker charge – and both sides were frankly horrible in a dour goalless draw the year before.

There has been acrimony over refereeing calls, not least the infamous Marcus Rashford non-offside that tipped the scales of a game in City's Treble-winning year. Haaland once kicked into gear in this fixture too. But the overriding feeling is that City rarely do themselves justice four miles away near Salford Quays.

When losing (in 2020, 2023 and 2026), City had all of the ball. Not a fair chunk, pretty much all of it. An average of 70 per cent – but they were eventually picked off by a team adept at counter-attacking rather than taking ownership of proceedings.

Bryan Mbeumo celebrates giving Manchester United the lead in the derby in January this year

Pep Guardiola's poor record at Old Trafford is one of the few things Enzo Maresca could feasibly improve upon

A mixture of doing little with possession, too pedestrian and risk averse, and then missing key defenders has generally done for them.

Remarkably, John Stones was injured for all three defeats. Ruben Dias missed the last two and in 2020, the absence of Aymeric Laporte was acutely felt.

That cocktail produces a sour taste and it is a strange quirk that the Emirates and Stamford Bridge are eminently happier hunting grounds for City.

The anaemic displays at Old Trafford almost mirror the diminishing lustre of this fixture and on Thursday, it was a decade to the day since Guardiola travelled to meet Jose Mourinho’s United for the very first time and Manchester took its place as the epicentre of the world game.

The anticipation ahead of that meeting has not been matched anywhere in the intervening years.

Maybe there is a responsibility on the current incumbents to bring back some vigour. Not off the pitch, not the media barbs, because neither appear interested in those, but in the style of the show, a blood-and-thunder that once was a prerequisite.

Carrick is unlikely to be able to engineer that this time, given United’s start to the season. Maresca, though, possesses a chance to continue the feeling of building a team in his image, to piggyback on the sense of achievement from Porto.

The little brawl in the tunnel will not have done them any harm at all in that respect. The way they defend will offer spaces for the likes of Bruno Fernandes to exploit but City are also creating heaps of chances.

‘Maresca has brought so much energy,’ says City's Matheus Nunes of his manager (pictured). ‘I feel like there is a new energy around. I think we needed that'

‘He (Maresca) has brought so much energy,’ said Matheus Nunes. ‘I feel like there is a new energy around. I think we needed that.

'He came with a lot of enthusiasm, he knows the standards of the club as he was here before and won everything. He’s got everything he needs to succeed, and I hope this season shows it.’

That has transmitted to the players. It is self-evident in the way they have talked and behaved over the first month. Most of them are looking for a first win at United and those sort of firsts can galvanise the older guard.

City go to their old foes with the fire to change the record.

Sports.title: ESPN under-fire over 'unprofessional' botched US Open graphic of Serena and Venus Williams
Sports.content:
Tennis fans were furious to see a botched ESPN graphic that was supposed to include photos of both Venus and Serena Williams.

'I think ESPN just threw up a graphic using two pictures of Serena????' one eagle-eyed fan wrote on X. 'Whoops.'

The graphic was intended to depict the five American women of the Open Era with the most victories in major singles matches before their 23rd birthday.

That list is topped by Venus Williams at 107, thanks to a professional career that began when she was just 14. Serena, who also turned pro at 14, ranked second with 103 wins before turning 23, followed by Mary Joe Fernandez (93), Chris Evert (90) and Coco Gauff (89).

Unfortunately for ESPN, Venus was not pictured. Instead, the graphic included two different photos of Serena alongside the images of Fernandez, Evert and Gauff.

'[ESPN] please do better,' one fan wrote on X. 'This is unprofessional.'

Tennis fans were furious to see a botched ESPN graphic during the ongoing US Open

Serena (right) and Venus (left) lost their first-round doubles match at Flushing Meadows

'For how bad ESPN is, they should be embarrassed over this,' another added on the r/tennis subreddit.

One fan joked that Ben Shelton's five-set quarterfinal win over reigning champion Carlos Alcaraz probably deprived ESPN's graphics department of any sleep. That match ended at 3.33am.

The Williams sisters were back in action at the US Open this year. Serena and Venus suffered defeat following a three-hour battle against Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching in their first-round doubles matchup at the Grand Slam on Friday night.

In the wake of the loss, the 23-time Grand Slam champion wasn't sticking around to savor her return to Flushing Meadows.

Serena 'fled the scene' leaving her sister and playing partner behind, according to tennis insider Ben Rothenberg.

She reportedly walked off the Arthur Ashe court, out of the stadium and straight into a car that was waiting to whisk her away into the New York City night.

In her haste to escape, Serena is said to have ditched Venus, who had headed to the locker room post-match, as is customary for players.

What's more, Rothenberg reported that Venus may have been amenable to speaking to the media but instead, Serena's hasty exit saw the duo skip post-match press.

The superstar siblings were obligated to speak to the press following their grueling showdown against Joint and Chan after multiple members of the media requested them. However, tournament officials opted against fining either of the fabulously wealthy tennis legends.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly is on the brink of leaving Chelsea and selling his minority stake - with Behdad Eghbali's Clearlake Capital set to take control of club
Sports.content:
Behdad Eghbali and his Clearlake Capital group could soon have total control over Chelsea with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter believed to be progressing in talks to sell their minority shares.

Boehly, Walter and Hansjorg Wyss own 38.5 per cent of the Premier League club collectively. The other 61.5 per cent is held by Clearlake, who are led by Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano.

While Boehly is Chelsea chairman and was the original face of the 2022 takeover, Eghbali has been the most hands-on of all the co-owners. He often liaises with the sporting directorship team and is a consistent attendee at games both at home and away.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg, a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is likewise expected to sell. Wyss’s stance is unconfirmed.

If all three agreed to an in-house sale, Boehly, Walter and Wyss would expect to make a minor profit on their original investment. The entire consortium purchased Chelsea for £2.5billion in 2022 with an additional £1.75bn committed to investment in the club.

As originally reported by Bloomberg, a spokesperson for Walter said: ‘This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him. After this exit, Mr Walter intends to make future sports-related investments.’

Todd Boehly is believed to be progressing in talks to sell his minority share in Chelsea

Boehly's fellow minority owner Mark Walter is also doing similar, meaning Behdad Eghbali (pictured left with Boehly) and his Clearlake Capital group could have full control of the club

The spokesperson added: ‘Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time.’

Boehly tried his hand at being involved in transfers early on – he once admitted to buying Marc Cucurella from Brighton because Manchester City also wanted him – though Eghbali has largely led the show since that early experiment.

Reports have suggested Boehly and Eghbali held a strained relationship and there has been speculation surrounding one buying out the other for around two years now.

Sports.title: Man United make light work of minnows Sabah as Youri Tielemans excels in 4-0 win on Champions League return - but tougher tests await for Michael Carrick's men
Sports.content:
Until the Champions League anthem echoed around Old Trafford for the first time in nearly three years shortly before kick-off here last night, it was easy to forget that playing Sabah on a Thursday night marked Manchester United's return to Europe's top table.

With respect to the visitors from Azerbaijan, it was a fixture and a night of the week more in keeping with the UEFA Conference League.

United duly made light work of the minnows from Masazir – population 19,000 – to get their campaign off to the winning start that everyone expected and maintain a 100 per cent record among Premier League clubs in this week's first round.

The timing of the game, three days before the Old Trafford derby, was not ideal for Michael Carrick given that Manchester City had played on Tuesday.

However, a routine win and the opportunity to make changes both before and during this game with Sunday in mind was just what Carrick needed.

Safe to say, a decidedly tougher test awaits United away to Atletico Madrid in the Metropolitano next month.

Youri Tielemans (left) excelled on Manchester United's return to the Champions League

Benjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring on his first start of the season

It's difficult to judge their performance against opposition of this quality, but Youri Tielemans – whose £35million transfer fee from Aston Villa this summer could have paid for the Sabah squad twice over – excelled in midfield to help put the result beyond doubt before half-time, and Kobbie Mainoo shone alongside him.

MATCH STATS AND PLAYER RATINGS

MAN UTD (4-2-3-1): Lammens 6.5; Mazraoui 7, Yoro 6.5, Martinez 7, Dorgu 7 (Amass 72, 6); Mainoo 7.5 (Santos 64, 6), Tielemans 8 (Mount 46, 6); Mbeumo 6.5 (Lacey 72, 6.5), B Fernandes 7, Cunha 7.5; Sesko 6.5 (Zirkzee 64, 7) Subs not used: Darlow, Mee, Dalot, Heaven, Maguire, T Fletcher, Rashford. Scorers: Cunha 27, Fernandes 42, Sesko 45, Martinez 68 Booked: Dorgu Head coach: Michael Carrick 7 SABAH FK (4-2-3-1): Pokatilov 5; Zedadka 5 (Almeida 76, 6), Dashdamiro 6, McCarthy 6.5, Puchacz 5; Rakhmonaliev 5.5 (Khaibulaev 71, 6), Lepinjica 5; Parris 7 (Isaev 63, 5.5), Simic 6 (Du Queiroz 75, 5.5), Nwachukwu 4.5 (Mbina 46, 6); Mickels 7 Subs not used: Ramazanov, Mirzammadov, Rustamli, Mutallimov, R Fernandes, Mukhtarov Booked: Lepinjica Head coach: Valdas Dambrauskas 5 Referee: Willy Delajod (France) 7 Att: 73,685

Luke Shaw, on whom so much hinges at left-back, was rested after suffering cramp in last Sunday's draw at Everton, and his replacement Patrick Dorgu posed a persistent threat going forward, even though his defensive capabilities were rarely tested.

Marcus Rashford was also left on the bench after overstretching a hamstring at the weekend, which meant that Matheus Cunha reverted to the left flank after struggling as a false nine in the opening three games, and Benjamin Sesko made his first start of the season.

Both players scored here with Sesko's second goal in four days strengthening his case to be in the line-up against City.

'Of course, I'm happy with my goal,' said the Slovenian. 'I think the confidence boost is definitely big. Now it's important to recover well and focus on the derby.'

United could hardly have chosen a more peculiar occasion for their 300th appearance in this competition. They were 1/10 on with the bookies to beat a club that didn't even exist a decade ago and had already fought through four qualifying rounds as underdogs to reach the league phase.

The story of their manager Valdas Dambrauskas, retold many times before he arrived back in Manchester, rather summed up the remarkable nature of this tie. The man who won £2,500 on Lithuania's version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? and used it to fund a coaching education which included a spell with United's Soccer Schools.

It's fair to say that education continued on a night when Sabah gave a good account of themselves but always looked second best.

'I think we learned a lot,' admitted Dambrauskas. 'We will all go home thinking we could have done a little bit better, especially with the result.

'This is massive experience for us; 16 players went on the pitch and only one of them played at this level before.'

Matheus Cunha was on the end of Patrick Dorgu's cross to give United a 27th minute lead

Lisandro Martinez pounced to score from close range and complete the scoring at Old Trafford

The Sabah players were out on the grass more than an hour before the start, their excitement clear for all to see as they filmed themselves and took pictures.

Once the action started, they seemed undaunted by the occasion and the pace of Kaheem Parris and dangerman Joy Lance Mickels kept United's defence on its toes.

Not surprisingly, though, it was Carrick's side who made the better chances including two early opportunities on the right side of the box for Cunha and Noussair Mazraoui.

Two Tielemans passes led to Bruno Fernandes narrowly failing to find Sesko in front of goal as Rahman Dashdamirov intercepted, and Bryan Mbeumo cutting in from the right to fire straight at goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov before United made the breakthrough in the 27th minute.

Sabah were over-committed when an attack broke down close to half-way and they were punished. Mbeumo seized on the loose ball and it went through Sesko and Fernandes before Dorgu's first-time cross picked out Cunha whose close-range finish found its way past Pokatilov.

The man who couldn't score through the middle hadn't taken long to profit in his preferred position on the left side of United's attack.

While the lead was only one, Sabah were always in with a chance. They got closer to Senne Lammens' goal on occasions than Carrick would have liked, not least when Mickels headed into the side-netting from Parris' cross to the far post.

But United effectively killed the game off with two goals in the space of three minutes before half-time.

The first of them was created by Tielemans who started the move and then continued his run into the box to receive Cunha's pass, spinning cleverly to set up Fernandes for a clinical first-time finish.

Then the United captain broke from halfway and fed Mbeumo who slid a pass into the path of Sesko who rounded Pokatilov to score.

With the game all but won, you couldn't blame Carrick for taking off Tielemans at half-time to protect the Belgian ahead of the City game on Sunday. Mainoo and Sesko soon followed, and the changes continued after United made it 4-0 in the 68th minute.

Pokatilov fumbled a close-range effort from substitute Joshua Zirkzee, and Lisandro Martinez pounced to score from close range.

Credit to Sabah, they kept going and Mickels flashed a shot wide before Orphe Mbina headed against the bar in added time.

But having embarrassingly gone out at the group stage in 2023, United's first venture into the new league phase has gone smoothly.

Now it's onto the Metropolitano, which will host the Champions League final in June. It's far too early to say if United have even the slightest chance of being there, and games like this won't give us a clue either way.

Sports.title: Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend 'hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers while sleeping in their Paris flat'
Sports.content:
Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend 'hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers while sleeping in their Paris flat'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend suffered a terrifying break-in in Paris in 2023, a court was told.

The Man City goalkeeper and Alessia Elefante, whom he has since married and had a child with, were hit, bound and threatened with a knife after robbers broke into their flat.

The incident took place in Avenue Montaigne, one of Paris' most famous and luxurious streets, with Donnarumma and his partner asleep at the time.

The keeper, 27, was then at PSG, and a Paris criminal court is currently conducting a two-day hearing about the ordeal.

Donnarumma is not expected to give evidence but a witness statement from him shed further light on what went on.

Court documents revealed how Donnarumma was woken by a man saying 'shh', before he was hit in the face with a knuckle duster and threatened with a knife.

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend Alessia Elefante were hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers in their Paris flat in 2023 (pictured together in 2024)

The thieves left with keys to supercars, cash, watches and luxury handbags after robbing Donnarumma and Elefante (pictured in 2024)

The man then said: 'The watches, the watches'.

As per court documents, Donnarumma replied: 'I showed him the one on the dressing table, an Audemars Piguet.' Those watches can have a value worth up to hundreds of thousands of euros.

His partner told investigators that she was also woken up by the thieves who attacked her and shouted: 'The money, the watches.'

She subsequently gave them a Cartier watch, jewellery and €2,000 (£1718) in cash.

Elefante was then accosted for the code to a safe. However, she revealed she didn't know it and said it was empty anyway.

'They got angry thinking that I was lying,' she told investigators. 'They pulled me by the hair and one of them hit me on the thighs. I said I was pregnant but they continued.'

Donnarumma did then give them the code to the safe, but as Elefante had warned, there was nothing in there.

The court was told that the robbers left with keys to a Mercedes and a Lamborghini, cash, watches and luxury handbags.

Police also added that the four robbers managed to get into the flat by using a ladder to climb onto the roof, before they lowered themselves onto the balcony and broke in through windows.

Two individuals that are already in prison - Ilyas Kherbouch, a 21-year-old with at least 11 criminal convictions, and Khyan Mamouni - are accused of masterminding and ordering the robbery from their cells. They both deny the charges.

Kherbouch, who escaped from jail in March and spent 13 days on the run, caused a stir at the opening of the trial.

This came when he insulted and threatened police officers when they told his brother to leave the court.

'Come here, you,' he told them. 'What are you going to do?'

When warned that he could be expelled from the courtroom, he replied: 'I couldn’t care less. I don’t want to be present at the trial. I don’t give a s***.'

Donnarumma, now 27 and at Man City, was playing for PSG at the time of the terrifying ordeal

Two of the robbers, who were under the age of 18 when the incident happened, have already been given jail sentences of three and four years respectively at a children's court.

Another defendant Moktar Diop, 24, admitted to taking part but is not accused of resorting to violence, while a fourth suspect died by suicide in 2024. He had previously admitted to being involved but told investigators he had come under pressure from his accomplices.

Donnarumma and his partner's lawyers said previously that they were 'still profoundly shocked'.

The trial continues.

Sports.title: Pakistan endure another day of despair as miserable tour continues: This once great cricketing nation has been reduced to chaos and cluelessness as England close in on series whitewash, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Moments after Ollie Robinson, immovable from the crest of his wave, had Saim Ayub caught in the slips by Harry Brook from the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings, a PA announcement warned Edgbaston stewards of a ‘Code Red’.

It had apparently been triggered by a fire alarm and, for a few seconds, the crowd fell eerily silent. But they burst into life three balls later when Robinson had Abdullah Shafique poking low to Joe Root at first slip, leaving the tourists nought for two and facing a Code Red situation of their own.

The fire alarm proved false, and Pakistan saved at least a little face by reaching 52 for two before rain ended play shortly after 5pm.

But as Root’s team closed in on a 3–0 whitewash in gloomy Birmingham, it was possible to feel two emotions at the same time: delight for England, who batted with panache and bowled with precision, and despair for Pakistan, a once great side reduced to chaos and cluelessness by the machinations of their board and the misery of their players.

There was uproar in Karachi and Lahore when, only two days into this series, their side were described as the worst their country had sent to these shores for 50 years. Those voices have fallen silent now, with England – in disarray themselves not long ago – largely doing as they pleased on the second day of this third and final Test.

Resuming on 156 for four, they thrashed 297 in 60 overs before being dismissed for 453, at which point Robinson took his series haul to 21 wickets at an average of 6.66 with the kind of precision that turns metronomes green with envy. It has all been closer to bloodsport than sport.

Ollie Robinson shone again as England closed in on a series whitewash over Pakistan

It was another day of despair for Pakistan as their miserable tour of England nears an end

We should be careful what we wish for, of course. Until recently, the idea of England winning every Test of a series would have been greeted with a snort of derision. But while they deserve credit for keeping their foot on Pakistan’s throat, the one-sidedness of the cricket has raised more questions about a format that rarely stops fretting over its future.

It’s no good grumbling about the unfettered growth of the T20 franchise circuit when Test cricket is properly contested by only a handful of nations. And it’s no good wondering why this inequality has been allowed to arise when the bigger nations shrug their shoulders at the ICC’s lopsided financial model, and the ICC themselves turn a blind eye to the game’s growing politicisation.

As this tour has confirmed, Pakistan are on the wrong side of each of these debates, with the chairman of their cricket board, Mohsin Naqvi, doubling up as the country’s interior minister, and presiding over the farcical culling of almost half their squad between Lord’s and Edgbaston.

It all meant the day proceeded along predictable lines, with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence sniffing out any prospect of a Pakistani comeback by taking 73 from the morning’s first 10 overs while barely breaking sweat.

But if there has been one criticism of England, it has been the failure of their batsmen to convert starts into something more meaningful, and here again they promised more than they delivered.

Brook had struck the perfect tempo in moving to 75 in three and a quarter hours when he pushed an off-break from Ayub towards midwicket and set off for a single even as Shan Masood swooped on the ball, before running him out comfortably at the non-striker’s end.

Might Lawrence reach three figures instead? Moments before lunch, he contrived to chop a widish delivery from Mohammad Imran on to his stumps, and walked off in anguish for 65. Three half-centuries in four innings since his recall have been a good return, but the battle for top-six places is cranking up. This was an opportunity missed.

Jamie Smith, batting with a dislocated left index finger sustained in the field on the first day, played some meaty strokes for his third sixty in five innings, only to provide a simple return catch off a leading edge to Razaullah.

And while Robinson hit out for his second Test fifty, his dismissal left England with 21 half-centuries from six games this summer, and a lone hundred, by Ben Duckett against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

Unless one of Pakistan’s batsmen can go big tomorrow, this will be the first Test series in England of three matches or more not to feature an individual century since the 1888 Ashes.

Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence were two of five England batsmen to pass 50 in their innings

This Pakistan side are one of the worst touring teams to ever come to here for a Test series

Not that any of this troubled Robinson as he performed his now customary demolition of Pakistan’s top order.

Ayub’s most recent cricket had been for Jamaica Kingsmen in the Caribbean Premier League, which most sensible set-ups might think was no kind of preparation for red-ball cricket under grey English skies. Sure enough, he completed a pair by wafting hopelessly at his first ball.

Cox, keeping in place of the injured Smith, now came up to the stumps for Shafique, who poked at Robinson as if in a trance. Since making 61 at Headingley, Shafique has managed 23 in five innings, and been dismissed in five of his six by Robinson.

Duckett put down a slip catch for the third time in the game when Shan Masood flashed at the luckless Gus Atkinson, while Jofra Archer lacked his usual menace. But such is the gulf between the sides that England can afford these blemishes and still win this game at a canter.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence says Ollie Robinson is 'at the peak of his powers' after England bowler continues remarkable series against Pakistan - and gives verdict on own position in team
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson is operating at the ‘peak of his powers’ and making his England team-mates believe he will take a wicket every ball.

That was the assessment from the slip cordon of Dan Lawrence, after Robinson struck twice in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings at Edgbaston.

‘When he's bowling, when he's putting it in the same spot pretty much every ball, you certainly do feel in the game behind the stumps, especially when you've got someone pretty much at the peak of his powers,’ said Lawrence.

Robinson’s double strike took his series wickets tally to an astonishing 21 at a cost of just 6.66 runs each.

Bad weather ended play prematurely, leaving a Pakistan team yet to make 200 in five previous innings on 52 for two and requiring 268 more runs to make Joe Root’s England bat again.

At the other end of the day, Surrey’s Lawrence dominated the early scoring in a rapid start alongside Harry Brook, but like his fifth-wicket partner failed to turn a half century into a hundred, finishing with 65 off 82 balls, in a score of 453.

Dan Lawrence heaped praise on Ollie Robinson after he continued his remarkable series

Lawrence, who earlier scored 65, said the England bowler was 'at the peak of his powers'

With three 50s in four innings, the 29-year-old might have done enough to maintain his place in the squad for the winter tour of South Africa. Jacob Bethell will be back from knee surgery by then and Sam Curran has been nominated as Ben Stokes’ successor in the all-rounder role. The rest will be determined over the next fortnight.

Incoming coach Stephen Fleming is scheduled to arrive next week and is understood to be keen on getting around the country, talking to directors of cricket and coaches about the country’s leading players.

‘In regards to position in the team, only the selectors and the captain will know that, and I'm pretty happy with how I've contributed and we'll see what happens,’ Lawrence said.

‘I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against a tiring attack. I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest, but it wasn't meant to be.’

Surrey team-mate Jamie Smith and Robinson also made half centuries, although the former was unable to take his place behind the stumps due to a dislocated finger.

Jordan Cox will keep wicket for the remainder of a contest that appears destined to finish on Friday, marking the beginning of the post-Bazball era with a 3-0 whitewash.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Declan Rice makes risky comment as 'rusty' star called out
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Declan Rice makes risky comment as 'rusty' star called out

Arsenal fans could hit back after Declan Rice's post-Napoli comments

View 3 Images Declan Rice's allegiance is clear after his latest comment (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Arsenal's successful start to their Champions League campaign was followed by a questionable decision by Declan Rice. The Premier League champions claimed a 1-0 win away to Napoli on Wednesday, courtesy of Martin Odegaard's second-half goal.

‌



The Gunners captain continued his strong start to the season with his winning strike at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, marking his fourth goal of the campaign. Mikel Arteta's side will hope to go one step further in Europe this time round, following their final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

‌



The aftermath of Arsenal's triumph abroad saw Rice take a risky stance on the Ballon d'Or race, while one star who started the clash was deemed to have missed an opportunity to impress.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal icon calls out supporters and hints at Mikel Arteta transfer mistake READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta spotted 'raging' at three Arsenal stars during Napoli win READ MORE :

Rice snubs team-mates

View 3 Images Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba and Declan Rice were all nominated for the Ballon d'Or (Image: Shirlaine Forrest/Getty Images)

Rice has risked feeling the wrath of Arsenal fans after admitting he'd like to see Tottenham icon Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or. The midfielder was nominated for the award alongside fellow team-mates William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes after clinching the Premier League title last season.

‌



The Bayern Munich striker is among the favourites to win after scoring 61 goals for the club on the way to securing a second consecutive Bundesliga title. The England captain now has the backing of his international team-mate, who revealed his stance after Wednesday's victory.

Rice said: "Yeah for sure (I’m proud), second year in a row nominated, it’s obviously really good, I’m really proud. Obviously I know who I want to win it, I’d love to see Harry Kane win it, so I’m wishing him all the best in that. Kane has never won the Ballon d’Or, but this is surely as good a chance as he’s going to get."

Merino 'rusty' verdict

View 3 Images Mikel Merino started his first game of the season against Napoli (Image: Nicola Ianuale/Shutterstock)

‌



Mikel Merino earned his first start of the season in the victory against the Serie A side. The Spaniard returned to club duties late after winning the World Cup with team-mates David Raya and Martin Zubimendi.

He's since been eased back into the team in the opening weeks of the season and he's come off the bench in all three of Arsenal's league games, totalling 46 minutes of action. He played 65 minutes against Napoli and his performance was labelled as "rusty" by Gunners icon Martin Keown.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick gives Luke Shaw injury update after he misses game before Manchester derby
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick gives Luke Shaw injury update after he misses game before Manchester derby

Luke Shaw was missing from the Manchester United squad for their 4-0 win against Azerbaijani side Sabah on Thursday night and Red Devils boss Michael Carrick has given an update

View 2 Images Luke Shaw was a notable omission vs Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has revealed Luke Shaw’s absence against Sabah on Thursday night was just a precaution. The defender was missing from the Red Devils’ squad for their comfortable 4-0 win in their Champions League opener at Old Trafford.

‌



But the United boss has assured fans that he wasn’t ruled out with a serious issue and his absence was just a precautionary measure ahead of this weekend’s derby clash with local rivals Manchester City.

‌



Speaking before Thursday evening’s game, Carrick said: "It's a little bit of that [managing him]. He came off the other day [at Everton] with a little bit of cramp.

‌



“We didn't want to take any risks really. We tried to manage him so we will see how he is after this one."

‌



Carrick reshuffled his side in the absence of Shaw, with Patrick Dorgu instead being selected at left-back. The Dane enjoyed a positive evening, having teed up Matheus Cunha for the Red Devils’ opener, while he also managed to help the side to their first clean sheet of the campaign.

He was also named the UEFA Player of the Match. Speaking after United’s emphatic win, Dorgu said: “It was good. Really thank you to god for the giving me the opportunity to play in the Champions League.

“I’m really happy with my performance and really happy that the team got the three points and are up and running in the Champions League.”

‌



He added: “The last couple of games, we conceded a lot of goals so it was good to get the confidence going into the derby at the weekend.”

View 2 Images Patrick Dorgu played a left back for Man United vs Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick was also able to give Dorgu a rest, with fellow defender Harry Amass handed a late cameo off the bench at left-back, having been left out of the squad for the 2-2 draw with Everton on the weekend.

‌



United boss Carrick was left satisfied with the Red Devils' ability to keep Sabah out. He said: "It's nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. There was a lot. I thought some of our attacking play was fantastic. Some of the football we played was really good, dangerous on transition.

"Defended on the most part really well. I have to give them [Sabah] a lot of credit. A really tough team to play against. They play little connections and make you really work to get the ball back. The result looks comfortable, it wasn't always like that. I thought we did a lot of good things tonight which gave us a good result."

Sports.title: Premier League star admits he would CYCLE to Man Utd after transfer collapse
Sports.content:
Premier League star admits he would CYCLE to Man Utd after transfer collapse

Manchester United chose not to sign a new defender this summer but it appears that a former Bundesliga star would have accepted a move to Old Trafford had he been approached

View 2 Images Thomas Meunier penned a deal with Sunderland this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Sunderland star Thomas Meunier claims he would jump at the chance to sign for Manchester United - but is happy at the Stadium of Light. The Belgian defender joined the Black Cats on a free transfer this summer following his exit from Lille.

‌



A boyhood United fan, Meunier has said that he would have done anything to join the Red Devils, albeit is very happy with the choice he made.

‌



Speaking to Walfoot, the 34-year-old said: “You don’t always get to choose exactly where you want to go. Otherwise, I’d have gone to Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, or Manchester United! But seriously, they [Sunderland] called me and were incredibly convincing.

‌



“Their pitch was good. The conversation with the manager was, too: you spend an hour on the phone talking football, and you realize you’re dealing with a guy who simply loves the game—just like I do.

“And the fact that it was Sunderland… It just so happens there’s that documentary – Sunderland ‘til I Die – which I really enjoyed.”

On his affection for the Red Devils, the former Dortmund star added: “If they ever ask me, I’ll cycle there. (laughs). But maybe it’s better this way. Suppose I play there and have a bad time. I wouldn’t want to hate Manchester United, because I love that club so much.

“I went to watch them a few weeks ago, against Bilbao. In with the fans, singing, à fond (fully). Je suis un vrai. (I am a real one). I go to watch them at least once every season.

‌



“But of all the home games I’ve seen in all those years, they’ve only won two. You have to have a self cruelty side to be a United supporter, right?”

View 2 Images Thomas Meunier is a boyhood Man United fan (Image: Getty Images)

Ironically, Meunier seemingly had the chance to sign for his boyhood club in the past, only to pass up on the chance due to an unspecified coach encouraging him to sign a deal with his agent first.

‌



Speaking last year, he said: "When I was at Dortmund. I could have signed for Manchester United. I didn’t have an agent. And, in fact, the coach there at the time clearly directed me to his agent so I could sign for Manchester United. I refused, and I didn’t sign. Otherwise, you would have known… But there you go.”

“That’s also the negative side of football," he added. "There’s a lot of money at stake. And even coaches work with agents specifically to place players and get paid. I have 45 examples like that. Now, I can’t prove them all, so I won’t name any names. But it’s something that, in my opinion, still happens far too frequently.”

Sports.content:
The 'UK's Hardest Man' makes four-word promise before Jordan McCann fight

The 'UK's Hardest Man' - Big Stacks - will finally settle his bitter feud with long-time rival Jordan McCann over in Newcastle in a Misfits clash this weekend

View Image Big Stacks ahead of his fight (Image: DAZN)

The 'UK's Hardest Man' - commonly known as Big Stacks - has promised to quit social media and enter the 9-5 life should he suffer an embarrassing defeat to Jordan McCann on Saturday night.

‌



Big Stacks and McCann will settle their bitter feud in a mouthwatering clash this weekend in Newcastle. Their rivalry stemmed from a physical altercation back in June, which saw McCann - who was fighting the Ibiza Final Boss - punch Stacks at an open workout event before a Misfits show.

‌



Security were quick to intervene, but the brawl left Stacks with a busted lip. The scuffle meant that the 'Hardest Man' was involved in a rather comical ‘bodyshots only’ bout against Armz Korleone. Stacks would eventually go on to lose the contest.

‌



After trading verbal blows in the weeks that followed, the Misfits brass were eager to pit the pair against each other. On Thursday evening, Big Stacks and McCann went head-to-head at a pre-fight press conference, and it did not take long before they were at each other's throats.

Sports.title: Barcelona chief Deco confirms interest in Liverpool star after impressive performance
Sports.content:
Barcelona chief Deco confirms interest in Liverpool star after impressive performance

Liverpool star Ronald Araujo has already secured a spot in the starting XI following his summer switch to Anfield but Barcelona are continuing to keep a close eye on him

View 2 Images Deco has given his thoughts on Ronald Araujo's performances with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Barcelona chief Deco has confirmed he is keeping his fingers crossed for Ronald Araujo at Liverpool. The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan move over the closing days of the transfer window.

‌



Liverpool have a £47million option to make the move permanent. Araujo, 27, has already impressed having made four appearances for his new employers and he has played the full 90 minutes in victories against Ipswich and Atletico Madrid.

‌



Having tuned into the Reds’ win against the Spanish side, Barcelona sporting director Deco has suggested he is hoping Araujo continues to shine at Anfield, although he stopped short of suggesting whether he would be moving permanently.

‌



“I watched the Liverpool match yesterday,” he told Spanish outlet Sport. “I love him. I’m fond of him and want him to succeed. Personally, I love him. At times, he hasn’t been able to play at his usual level.

“His time at Barça was spectacular. Sometimes, ideas don’t align. He is under contract with us; it’s still early days.”

Deco is not the only one to have spoken out on Araujo’s performances at Anfield so far. Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has also given his taken and has been impressed.

“I think he’s been very, very good. [He was] the other day and I would say he’s been even better today,” he said after the win against Atletico Madrid. “I think he’s defending his side really well, and also sometimes, because he’s a centre-back, we underrate his offensive side.

‌



“Today he gives a great assist to Dom Szoboszlai, he’s made a couple of very good serves from his position. I’m very happy with him, very happy.

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo has had a bright start to life with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

“He’s come with the willingness to show that he belongs at this level, and I hope we can keep him there, because he’s in a lovely place.”

‌



Araujo has also given an insight into his start to life with Liverpool. He said: "We've got a great team and, little by little, we're growing too - meeting all the coach's demands and reaching a higher level. Liverpool is a big club like Barcelona. I'm working hard, as you can see also on the pitch. I am happy here and hungry for more.

"Liverpool are a great club and I'm really looking forward to continuing to give my all so I can keep contributing to the team."

He added: "I love playing in this stadium. It's a very special and lovely place, and when we're also able to show off all our hard work here with a good result, it makes us feel very satisfied. We were up against a great opponent, who we knew had already had some good nights here, but we stood up to them, played a great match and came away with the win, which was the important thing."

Sports.title: All 25 managers sacked by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis as he axes another
Sports.content:
All 25 managers sacked by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis as he axes another

The number of managers let go by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis has reached the quarter-century mark

View 5 Images It's fair to say Evangelos Marinakis is trigger happy (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Deaths, taxes and Evangelos Marinakis sacking a manager every few months are three of life's certainties. The colourful Nottingham Forest owner has been at it again.

‌



No, Oliver Glasner remains in situ at the City Ground despite a sluggish start to the season for Forest. The Greek shipping magnate has swung the axe at one of his other clubs, Olympiacos, sacking Jose Luis Mendilibar, the man who led the club to Conference League glory in 2024.

‌



Mendilibar has been dismissed despite not losing a match inside 90 minutes so far this season. Olympiacos are a respectable third in the Greek top flight, two points behind bitter early leaders Panetolikos.

‌



He becomes the 25th manager to be dismissed by Marinakis, who also owns Portuguese side Rio Ave, across his three clubs. Here's a round-up…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Nottingham Forest (took over in 2017)

Mark Warburton (sacked December 2017): After helping Forest avoid relegation to the third tier in 2016/17, he was axed nine months into a two-and-a-half-year contract.

‌



Aitor Karanka (mutual termination, January 2019): This was more of a mutual separation after the Spaniard fell out with Marinakis with Forest seventh in the Championship table.

Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner READ MORE :

Martin O'Neill (sacked June 2019): Not even a Forest European Cup-winning legend was safe. O'Neill was let go after just five months after reportedly falling out with players.

Sabri Lamouchi (sacked October 2020): The Frenchman lasted an impressive (by Marinakis' standards) 15 months, almost leading Forest into the Championship play-offs in 2020. Four games and four defeats into the following season, Lamouchi was given his marching orders.

‌



Chris Hughton (sacked September 2021): After guiding Forest to safety in 2020/21, the veteran boss paid the price for six defeats in seven games.

Steve Cooper (sacked December 2023): The Welshman led Forest to promotion to the Premier League in 2022, ending a 23-year absence from the top flight, and then kept them up the following season. However, a run of five defeats in six games saw him given the boot.

Nuno Espirito Santo (sacked September 2025): The respected Portuguese boss had guided Forest to seventh place and European football just a few months earlier. But the appointment of Edu as head of global football was the beginning of the end. Nuno speaking out against his boss didn't help matters either and he was sacked just three games into last season. Meanwhile, Edu formally left the club earlier this month.

‌



View 5 Images The relationship between Marinakis and Nuno turned sour (Image: Getty Images)

Ange Postecoglou (sacked October 2025): Going from a conservative coach to an all-out attacking one looked questionable at the time. And so it proved with the Aussie lasting just 39 days.

Sean Dyche (sacked February 2026): The dream job became a nightmare for the former Forest trainee. Results weren't actually that bad but after Marinakis consulted the players, he opted to swing the axe again - this time on a 114-day reign.

‌



Vitor Pereira (left in July 2026 after mutual termination clause triggered): Despite steering Forest to safety and the semi-finals of the Europa League, the Portuguese coach was let go and replaced by Glasner.

View 5 Images Sean Dyche was given his marching orders during a chaotic 2025/26 season (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

Olympiacos (took over in 2010)

Ewald Lienen (sacked August 2010): The head coach was shown the door after Olympiacos were surprisingly knocked out of the Europa League in the third qualifying round by Maccabi Tel-Aviv.

‌



Leonardo Jardim (sacked January 2013): After replacing Ernesto Valverde, who had resigned, Jardim was sacked despite Olympiacos being well clear at the top of the table.

Michel (sacked January 2015): After a whopping two years at the helm, the Spaniard may have been thinking about a testimonial. Instead, despite a run of five runs in a row, he was brutally sacked.

Victor Sanchez (sacked August 2016): Marco Silva's successor was axed after less than two months in charge following the team's failure to reach the Champions League group stage.

‌



Paulo Bento (sacked March 2017): You'd think topping the league by seven points would be enough to keep a manager in a job, wouldn't you? Nope. Bento was gone just seven months after taking charge.

View 5 Images Topping the league wasn't good enough for Paulo Bento (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

Besnik Hasi (sacked September 2017): The Serbian got the chop following a defeat to local rivals AEK Athens. He was in charge for just 109 days.

‌



Takis Lemonis (sacked January 2018): Lemonis' fourth reign at the club was ended by Marinakis, who thought the grass was greener elsewhere.

Oscar Garcia (mutual consent April 2018): Perhaps realising he wasn't working in the most stable of environments, Garcia decided to walk away with the club's blessing before the end of the season.

Pedro Martins (sacked August 2022): Despite having just penned a two-year extension, Martins was given his cards after losing a Champions League qualifier.

‌



Carlos Corberan (sacked September 2022): Another blink-and-you-missed reign, which lasted barely seven weeks. Corberan was soon back in the dugout with West Brom.

View 5 Images Carlos Corberan swapped Athens for the West Midlands (Image: Adam Fradgley/West Bromwich Albion FC via Getty Images)

Diego Martinez (sacked December 2023): One of the more understandable sackings. Martinez was let go with the team sitting fourth in the table.

‌



Carlos Carvalhal (sacked February 2024): A 2-0 defeat to arch rivals Panathinaikos did for Carvalhal after two months at the helm.

Rio Ave (took over in 2023)

Luis Freire (sacked November 2024): After four years in charge, he was sacked with the team 14th in the league after 10 games.

Petit (contract not renewed in summer 2025): Despite guiding the team to an 11th-place finish and the last four of the domestic cup, the club opted not to renew his contract.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
